sentences.text: The primary privacy risks associated with this application are related to: Data minimization Confidentiality Security
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: When submitting an inquiry to the Ombudsman's Office, an inquirer may put data at risk by providing additional or unnecessary PII.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The Office mitigates this risk by limiting the scope of information collected in Entellitrak to the amount of data necessary to act upon inquiries.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: PII, limited to first name and last name, is used solely by the Ombudsman's Office to assist with resolving an inquiry.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Any additional PII submitted by the inquirer is not included in the Entellitrak record.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The information is collected directly from an inquirer, and the submission and collection of PII is voluntary.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The collection of this data is the minimum necessary amount of information for the Ombudsman's Office to assist an inquirer with resolving the inquiry.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Given the sensitive nature of inquiries received by the Ombudsman's Office, there is a risk of reputational harm to the inquirer, the Bureau, and the CFPB Ombudsman's Office in the event of a data breach or a breach of confidentiality.
sentences.heading: Confidentiality

sentences.text: The Bureau minimizes risk by enforcing access controls to minimize the access to data to only authorized Ombudsman's Office staff.
sentences.heading: Confidentiality

sentences.text: Ombudsman's Office staff are also trained on appropriate uses of the data within the application prior to receiving access to the application.
sentences.heading: Confidentiality

sentences.text: Entellitrak does not connect with any other application or system.
sentences.heading: Confidentiality

sentences.text: Given the content and sensitivity of information held within this cloud-based solution there is a risk that unauthorized individuals can gain access to the information via web interface.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The Bureau mitigates this risk by only granting Entellitrak system access to authorized Ombudsman's Office staff who, based on their need to know, are restricted to the minimal amount of data required or appropriate to carry out their assigned job responsibilities.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Access to the system is granted solely by the System Owner, the Ombudsman's Office, and approved users are required to log into the application with a secure username and password.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: This access is restricted or terminated at the request of the Ombudsman's Office, as necessary, should the staff member no longer have a need to know the information, change job functions, be terminated, or resign.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Information within the application is subject to the appropriate technical, physical, and administrative controls implemented to address these risks, such as encryption for data maintained within the system.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: For example, National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST) controls families, including Identification and Authentication (IA) and Risk Assessment (RA), are implemented to restrict access to the information to authorized Ombudsman's Office Staff.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The technical, physical, and administrative controls implemented to limit uses of PII, secure the application, and minimize data to the amount necessary are appropriate for the purpose of the application.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the Dodd-Frank Act), Public Law No. 111-203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Bureau administers, enforces, and implements federal consumer financial protection laws, and, among other powers, has authority to protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, and abusive practices related to consumer financial products or services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One of the primary functions of the Bureau under the Dodd-Frank Act is collecting, investigating, and responding to consumer complaints.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 The Bureau is also tasked with analyzing complaints to identify trends in service delivery to consumers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To fulfill these obligations, the Bureau created the Office of Consumer Response (Consumer Response) to: Answer consumers' questions Handle consumers' complaints Analyze and share complaint data and insights Consumer Response engages directly with consumers to understand the challenges they face in the financial marketplace and responds to their inquiries about consumer financial products and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer Response receives complaints about financial products and services from consumers via the Bureau's website, ConsumerFinance.gov/complaint/, by phone, physical mail, and email.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 2 In addition, the Bureau receives complaints by referral from other government agencies, the White House, and Congressional offices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addressing a complaint or inquiry, Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the Bureau for further administrative action.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 Consumer complaints are submissions that express dissatisfaction with, or communicate suspicion of wrongful conduct by, an identifiable entity related to a consumer's personal experience with a financial product or service.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 2 As an operational matter for the purposes of establishing reasonable procedures for providing timely responses to consumer inquiries, the Bureau defines consumer inquiries as consumer requests for information-typically proffered by telephone-to its Office of Consumer Response about consumer financial products or services, the status of a complaint, an action taken by the Bureau, and often combinations thereof.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The consumer complaints or inquiries themselves (including records about the complaint, details and supporting documents/documentation) are collected by Consumer Response and maintained in the Consumer Response System (CRS), which is the Bureau system of record for these interactions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 3 Consumer Response, with vendor assistance, operates the Consumer Resource Center (CRC), to directly interact with consumers for the intake of complaints and to field inquiries.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: While the vendor supports intake by phone, its services also include intake of physical mail 4 and email.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To do this, the vendor provides contact center services with Consumer Guides 5 who work at both a secure physical location and remotely.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The contact center provides the following services and capabilities: Communicate with consumers using a variety of telephony services; 6 Scan and print documents submitted by consumers; Perform quality assurance (QA) reviews of data entered by Consumer Guides as they process documents and interact with consumers; Train Consumer Guides; and Facilitate workforce management (WFM) of Consumer Guides to ensure sufficient staffing to support services and capabilities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 7 3 For more information, please see the Consumer Response PIA, March 2013, found here: https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/201303_CFPB_PIA-Consumer-Response-System.pdf.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 4 This refers to digitization of physical mail, where complaints and other documents are sent by consumers to a designated Bureau address for the CRC, processed by vendor staff and immediately scanned into CRS for Bureau use and documentation.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 5 Consumer Guides are vendor staff working behalf of the Bureau, who are trained to process complaints and inquiries from consumers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: They interact directly with consumers if they choose to speak to a person when calling the CRC contact center.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 6 Telephony refers to technology that facilitates communication over long distances through voice, text messages, video calling and conferencing, voicemail, call recording and fax.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Specifically, when considering voice, this PIA refers to real time voice communications and their capture, including caller self-service, call routing for assisted services, call recording, and similar voice-type services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 7 WFM uses PII for identity verification of staff and the overall operation of the CRC.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: For example, the email of Bureau staff is used for authentication to obtain access to the CRC system to fulfill their duties.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The services provided by the vendor are conducted in a secure physical location and within a FedRAMP 8 compliant private cloud environment that connects with the Bureau's CRS for direct input, transmission, and viewing of consumer information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: During its activities processing complaints, the CRC and the applications that support its operations collect, process, store, and transmit consumers' submissions, which can include the consumers' personally identifiable information (PII) and PII of financial service providers, and its employees, as well as that of Bureau and vendor staff.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Among the expected PII that can be transmitted through the CRC are names, email addresses, mailing addresses, phone numbers, official identification numbers, copies of documents/records, and details provided by consumers in their complaints (i.e., account numbers, transaction information, etc.).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The collection, input, and storage of consumer information by the CRC is confined solely to the Bureau and vendor systems that compose the CRC.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CRC uses automated features, some of which feature artificial intelligence technology 9 to capture and process data (including PII) from its activities to monitor and enhance its operations.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This information includes metadata related to a consumer call received by the CRC, such as the date and time call was received, call time duration, how long a consumer was on hold, and the outcome of the call.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer complaint information and data (i.e., the contents of a complaint) is stored in the Bureau's CRS, with limited access to non-Bureau staff.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer Guides working in the CRC environment connect to the CRS to enter information collected from consumers and to access the information needed to assist the individual consumers they are helping.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: During an interaction with the contact center there is a risk that a consumer may disclose more information than necessary to a Consumer Guide for the service they are seeking.
sentences.heading: Consumer Interactions

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, the CRC leverages processes and controls that limit the amount of information required to be provided by a consumer.
sentences.heading: Consumer Interactions

sentences.text: For example, when a consumer calls the CRC for a status update on a complaint, the Consumer Guide asks for basic, non-sensitive information to verify the consumer's identity.
sentences.heading: Consumer Interactions

sentences.text: The Consumer Guide does not ask for Social Security Numbers (SSN) or other sensitive information to verify one's identity for services that do not need it.
sentences.heading: Consumer Interactions

sentences.text: Additionally, when intaking a complaint, the Consumer Guide is trained to only ask for the necessary information to complete the complaint form.
sentences.heading: Consumer Interactions

sentences.text: Privacy Impact Assessment August 04, 2025
sentences.heading: Salesforce Platform (Cloud Environment) v.2

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, Public Law No. 111-203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In executing its duties, the CFPB performs several consumer and stakeholder relationship management and internal employee collaboration activities through a variety of business processes that are supported by information technology (IT) systems and applications.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB uses Salesforce, Inc. (Salesforce) cloud services to modernize its IT portfolio, to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of its consumer service management business processes, and to decrease the cost of hardware and software required by traditional systems and applications to support those business processes.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce is an external, Platform as a Service (PaaS) cloud-based customer relationship management platform offering extensive options for configuring workflows, databases, forms, dashboards and reports, process modeling, and customizable user interfaces.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce provides a selection of 'out of the box' functionality and custom tools to build internal and external facing applications that support various efforts such as consumer engagement and outreach, relationship management processes, employee collaboration, and internal workflows.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce enables the CFPB to quickly and efficiently build secure applications that automate manual business processes.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These processes may involve the collection of personally identifiable information (PII) from consumers or other members of the public, external partners and stakeholders, and CFPB Staff.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The type and scope of PII collected varies depending on the CFPB use case.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB's use of Salesforce is authorized by Sections 1011, 1012, and 1021 of the Dodd-Frank Act.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addition, specific CFPB programs use and collect PII through Salesforce in accordance with legal authorities under which the programs operate.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Information in Salesforce is collected in accordance with and is compliant with the Paperwork Reduction Act, the Right to Financial Privacy Act, and the Privacy Act of 1974. The use of Salesforce as a third-party cloud environment is also subject to the terms and conditions set forth in CFPB's contract with Salesforce as the vendor, to include the provisioning of the environment, service level agreements for the ongoing maintenance of the environment, and licenses provided to the CFPB for use of the environment.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce manages CFPB's technical cloud infrastructure on behalf of the CFPB, including general cloud environment tools such as data storage, system computing resources (such as routers and firewalls, data centers), software maintenance (such as security patches and secure upgrades to the environment), and access management tools.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce provides access to its environment tools and services to CFPB to build systems and applications to facilitate customer service and business processes, including: The collection and use of data via phone, web forms, chats, and email, allowing the CFPB to quickly address consumer cases or complaints.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Integrated, prebuilt case management tools and capabilities allowing the CFPB to handle case management activities, such as scheduling of meetings and interviews.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ability to integrate data held within transitional data systems and databases, saving the CFPB time and resources otherwise spent on data migration activities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ability to build applications that the CFPB uses to automate Helpdesk ticket resolution, escalate consumer concerns and complaints, and address consumer issues and concerns.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Standardized data collection methods and processes, such as standardizing the format of mailing addresses and customization of form fields, to collect the same type and amount of data to reduce duplicative and incorrect information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: AppExchange, the suite of CFPB authorized internal and third-party tools offered within the environment to support system development, administration, maintenance, and data storage.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CFPB Salesforce data is hosted and stored in the Salesforce Government Cloud, which is a Compliant Cloud System with Agency Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) High Authorization.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce also integrates with other CFPB-authorized thirdparty cloud system environments for purposes such as the storage of data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The integration allows data within Salesforce to be archived and stored securely within other CFPB-authorized cloud environments to reduce the cost of data storage, scan data and documentation to determine threats such as viruses prior to upload, and system security logging and monitoring tools to ensure authorized access to the environment.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: All third-party cloud systems that connect with Salesforce are assessed according CFPB's assessment and authorization (A&A) processes to ensure risks are identified and mitigated prior to use.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Authorized CFPB program managers, business product and system owners, system developers and business analysts, and other internal CFPB stakeholders and users, can access Salesforce to leverage these technical capabilities to build systems and applications in a secure, consistent method.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Salesforce, and applications developed within Salesforce, are managed through the CFPB Enterprise Platforms Salesforce Center of Excellence (COE), CFPB Change Control Board (CCB) processes and A&A documentation, and addresses privacy relative to systems development to include functional requirements analysis, alternatives analysis, feasibility analysis, benefits/cost analysis, and privacy risk assessments.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB initially published this privacy impact assessment (PIA) in April 2022 and is updating the PIA to reassess its use of Salesforce and document the privacy protections that are in place for the PII collected, used, shared, and maintained by the CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This PIA also covers the use of the Salesforce Own solution that is used to archive, backup, and restore Salesforce data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The scope of this PIA is limited to the privacy risks and technical controls associated with the maintenance and use of data within the Salesforce platform.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The information of Bureau personnel that is collected for authentication purposes is covered under CFPB.014 Direct Registration and User Management System (DRUMS) System of Records Notice (SORN).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Specific use cases and applications developed within Salesforce, and the analysis of the collection and use of PII, are assessed and documented within application specific PIAs 1 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB's authority to collect specific information, and routine uses of those records, are identified in the associated SORN 2 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Program specific uses of data that require Paperwork Reduction Act approval are also documented within the corresponding application specific PIAs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB conducts PIAs on both programs and information technology systems, pursuant to the E-Government Act of 2002, Section 208 3 and in alignment with Office of Management and Budget 4 (OMB) guidance and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standards.

sentences.text: Salesforce provides an ability to collect, process, and store PII to support a variety of CFPB programs and business functions through the development of and management of applications within the cloud environment.

sentences.text: Privacy Risk : There is a risk that the CFPB may use data beyond the intended purpose of collection, and that disparate data sources may be combined and used in new ways that are not consistent with the initial collection.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Mitigation : The CFPB mitigates this risk by conducting program and application specific PIAs to assess the collection and uses of PII in accordance with the authority to collect PII.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: The CFPB addresses privacy implications during the development lifecycle of an application to ensure that this privacy risk is managed throughout the development lifecycle, and continuous monitoring on systems and applications to ensure the purpose of collection remains consistent.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Privacy Risk : There is a risk that data stored within another cloud environment may be accessed by an unauthorized individual or that a breach within the cloud environment may impact business operations within Salesforce.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Mitigation : The CFPB mitigates this risk by sharing Salesforce data only with systems that have achieved an Authority to Operate (ATO) based upon the CFPB assessment & authorization (A&A) processes.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Connections between other cloud environments is assessed by the CFPB to apply rolebased environment access controls to ensure the security and privacy of the interconnection.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Any proposed data sharing between the cloud environments is also assessed to ensure only authorized individuals can access data within Salesforce.

sentences.heading: Identity, Credential and Access Management (ICAM)

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the Act), Public Law No. 111203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB relies upon diverse information technology (IT) systems and applications used by CFPB staff and external parties to perform their duties.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CFPB implements a comprehensive Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) program to centrally manage access to these applications and systems, and to safeguard the data CFPB collects, uses, shares, and maintains.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ICAM program collects information to verify individuals' identities, establish a digital identification (ID), and grant privileged access to CFPB data to complete their responsibilities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ICAM program centrally manages all staff (i.e., employees, contractors, detailees, volunteers, and interns) identification, authentication, and access privileges to all CFPB systems.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It also manages the provisioning of access to CFPB IT resources by authorized external individuals.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ICAM program manages a suite of enterprise tools and applications to create and manage digital IDs and access to CFPB IT resources.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CFPB uses these tools to help reduce costs, manage IT security risk, enable new business opportunities, and improve compliance.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These tools and applications also support CFPB's alignment with functional areas mapped to the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Identity Capability functions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB ICAM program comprises three structural areas: Identity Governance and Administration - Monitors and ensures that user identities and access rights remain properly managed, secure, and monitored.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It also provides insight into who has access to systems and PII based upon a defined role and responsibility.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Authentication & Authorization - Verifies staff identity and limits what actions CFPB staff can perform after access is granted.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Privileged Access Management - Focuses on the protection of privileged accounts at the CFPB where elevated access to systems and PII is managed using CFPB Rules of Behavior (RoBs) and Privilege User Access Requests (PUA) within specific environments.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: RoBs and PUAs are approved by system owners.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Authorized CFPB program managers, business owners, system developers, system owners, and other internal CFPB users can access these tools and applications to support and manage the agency's identity management need, such as deployment of two-factor authentication methods, and provisioning restricted and temporary access to CFPB data and resources.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ICAM program requires the collection and use of personally identifiable information (PII) to operate, which is stored in a centralized identity management data hub.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The PII is collected from internal data sources, such as the CFPB Automated Background Investigation System (ABIS) 1 and external resources hosted by federal agencies such as HR Connect, USAccess, Active Directory, Login.gov, and from external individuals.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The ICAM program uses PII from these various sources to provision accounts, coordinate and execute access requests and approvals, automate onboarding, transfer access between systems, and review access permissions across the enterprise.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB uses the PII to verify an individual's identity and confirm they are cleared through the appropriate security or background (conducted by the appropriate federal agencies on behalf of CFPB), and thus authorized to access our IT systems and network.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The PII is also used to assign a single digital trusted identity, such as a username, to authenticate individuals when logging into CFPB system 2 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Additionally, the PII allows the ICAM program to verify individuals each time an attempt is made to log into an IT system and monitor and manage these digital identities at the request of an individual, or as approved by a system owner.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is conducting this privacy impact assessment (PIA) to assess the ICAM program's use of PII stored within the centralized data hub and used within the tools and applications to identify the associated privacy risks.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The scope of this PIA is limited to the privacy risks and technical controls related to the maintenance and use of PII to support ICAM program activities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Specific tools and applications, such as automated PUA forms, are used to analyze the collection and use of PII with each system and user requesting access and these processes are documented within system-specific PIAs such as the CFPB Automatic Background Investigation System.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB's authority to collect specific information and routine uses of those records are identified in the associated Systems of Records Notices (SORN) 3 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Program-specific uses of data that require Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) approval will also be documented within the corresponding system-specific PIAs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Records are maintained in accordance with the applicable records retention schedule and are generally subject to National Archive and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedules (GRS) GRS 1.1, GRS 1.2, GRS 2.1, GRS 2.2, GRS 2.3, GRS 2.4, GRS 2.5, GRS 2.7, GRS 5.6, GRS 5.7, and GRS 6.4 depending on the record type and the corresponding disposition of that record type, and as specified within applicable SORNs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 The Automated Background Investigation System (ABIS) https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_automated-background-investigation-system-abis-pia_2021-03.pdf 2 Or in the case of Login.gov, it creates a single digital trusted identity across multiple federal systems and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The PII used by the ICAM program is collected in accordance with the Dodd-Frank Act, Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD) 12, NIST Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201-3, Person Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors, January 2022, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) M-19-17, and the Privacy Act of 1974. Changes within the ICAM program, which includes all the tools and applications utilized within the program, are managed through CFPB Change Control Board (CCB) processes and A&A documentation and address privacy to include functional requirements analysis, alternatives analysis, feasibility analysis, benefits/cost analysis, and privacy risk assessments.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The primary privacy risks associated with PII are related to: Data Quality and Integrity Data Minimization Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information Security Accountability and Auditing.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The ICAM program itself collects a very little amount of PII directly from individuals.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: The majority of PII collected by the program comes from other systems, applications, and associated processes such as human resources, onboarding data, and other federal government ICAM programs such as Login.gov and USAccess.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: This presents a risk that PII may be inaccurate when sourced by the ICAM program.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: The ICAM program mitigates this through implementation of procedures such as two-factor authentication, where individuals must validate their identity by providing a 'thing they know' (such as a password or personal identification number), a 'possession' (such as an ID badge or token on a smartphone), 'something you are' (username or email), and/or location.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: In addition, the ICAM program reviews all access requests approved by system owners via PUAs to determine the type of access required.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: If information in the PUA does not match the information sourced by the ICAM program for verification, the individual is not granted access.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: 3 One of these SORNS includes the GSA/GOVT-7, HSPD-12 USAccess, which covers all participating agency employees, contractors and their employees, consultants, and volunteers who require routine, long-term access to federal facilities, information technology systems, and networks.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: See also OPM/GOVT-1, General Personnel Records; OPM Central-9, Personnel Investigations Records.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: PII collected by the ICAM program enables the CFPB to provision access to its systems and applications.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: PII is collected from internal data sources, such as the CFPB ABIS, external resources hosted by federal agencies such as HR Connect, USAccess, Active Directory, Login.gov, and from external individuals.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Each of these sources contain a varying amount of PII.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: As a result, there is the risk that the program may collect more PII than is necessary to grant access.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, the ICAM program utilizes digital forms that collect only the minimum amount of PII necessary from source systems to build a digital identity, verify an individual's identity, and grant access to CFPB systems.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Once these forms are completed, the ICAM program builds an individual's digital identity within a centralized data hub.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: When an individual receives a digital identity, access can then be assigned by the ICAM program.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: System and data access just first be approved by a CFPB system owner before access is provisioned by the ICAM program.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: If more than the necessary amount of PII is provided to the ICAM program, ICAM program staff removes unnecessary PII before using the data to conduct program activities.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Further, the ICAM program centrally manages the identities of individuals to prevent the need to continually collect PII to identify individuals for requested access to individual systems.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The ICAM program collects PII about all CFPB staff and authorized external individuals to provision access to CFPB IT resources.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The amount of information collected presents a risk that PII can be used for unauthorized purposes.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The ICAM program mitigates this risk through automated access requests processes, such as PUAs, that limit the amount of PII used to verify an identity and provision access to the system.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: As part of this process, the system owner is an approver, ensuring that the individual is approved for access before the ICAM program grants access to the system or application.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The ICAM program also does not share any PII with any unauthorized individual in accordance with cybersecurity and privacy policies.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Given the sensitivity of PII collected and used by the ICAM program, the program's tools and applications may be a target for unauthorized access.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, the ICAM program tools and applications are subject to the appropriate technical, physical, and administrative controls issued by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to identify, analyze, prioritize, and remediate risks.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Security and privacy controls are implemented to restrict access to PII to authorized individuals who support the ICAM program.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: CFPB also has implemented security tools that can be configured to scan ICAM systems to detect malware, phishing, spam, and unsafe links.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The ICAM program also uses audit logs to audit login attempts and other such events as specified by the CFPB's Cybersecurity Enterprise Standards Manual (CS-S-01) 4 .
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Finally, access to the ICAM program tools and applications is strictly reviewed, approved, and maintained by the ICAM program leadership.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The ICAM program must ensure that authorized CFPB personnel have the right access to the right CFPB resources based on their roles.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: There is a risk that the ICAM program may inadvertently mishandle the PII it collects from CFPB staff by sharing it with an unauthorized person due to a gap in knowledge of CFPB procedure.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: To ensure these risks are mitigated, the ICAM program must complete annual role-based training on identifying various CFPB roles and the accompanying access to be granted, handling CFPB PII, and information security.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: The training covers topics to ensure the ICAM program is equipped to run checks that certify a person has the right access in the right role and that this access does not inadvertently grant the individual access to other roles or to other systems.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: For all other CFPB users who have been granted access to CFPB systems, the CFPB 's RoB provides guidance and specific rules on the appropriate use of CFPB information systems for individuals.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: Users must review, acknowledge, and sign that they understand the CFPB's RoB.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: Users are also only authorized to receive the minimal level of access required to accomplish assigned core job functions.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: For example, individuals requiring administrator rights to a system where said rights would be considered above that of a normal user must complete the PUA request and undergo reviews and approvals before access is granted.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: Finally, internal new-hire and annual training and guidance for managing PII apply to all who work for the CFPB, including vendor staff.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: The training includes recognizing possible breaches of PII and how to report them.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: The ICAM program works with system owners and employs both automated and manual processes to review and validate continued access to CFPB systems and applications.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: Additionally, both internal and independent auditors hold the CFPB accountable for complying with CFPB policies and procedures related to the processing of PII.
sentences.heading: Accountability and Auditing

sentences.text: The CFPB is committed to taking swift and immediate action if we uncover any violations of law, policies, and procedures.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the Act), Public Law No. 111203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB administers, enforces, and implements federal consumer financial protection laws and protects consumers from unfair, deceptive, and abusive practices when obtaining consumer financial products or services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One of the CFPB's primary responsibilities is supervising entities that provide consumers with financial products or services, such as loans or deposit accounts.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB has supervisory authority over multiple depository entities with over $10 billion in assets and includes large banks, credit unions, and their affiliates.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It also has authority over nondepository entities including mortgage entities, brokers and servicers, payday lenders, and private education lenders 1 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB supervises entities by gathering and evaluating information, which can include PII, to determine if they are in compliance with federal consumer financial laws.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB uses the Supervision and Examination System (SES) to conduct its supervision activities and facilitates the collection and sharing of relevant information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CFPB also uses it as an information repository for compliance rating information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Outcomes from a supervisory activity can include an Examination Report, which contains a compliance rating that reflects the CFPB's assessment of the effectiveness of the institution's compliance management program to ensure compliance with consumer protection laws and regulations and reduce the risk of harm to consumers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The SES resides within the Salesforce 2 cloud platform and leverages the capabilities of the cloud architecture including the automated collection of information requests, concurrent collaboration between internal assessments, and tracking of document reviews during the examination process.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The SES established the CFPB Supervision Portal to facilitate the secure exchange of communication and files between external entities and state regulators.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Identification and provisioning of these entity representatives is completed within the SES application by limited sets of CFPB users designated with permissions to perform the provisioning.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Additionally, the SES securely connects to CFPB's Microsoft O365 3 SharePoint environment for further data processing and storage capabilities, centering around document management.
sentences.heading: Overview
Overview

sentences.text: 2 See https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_salesforce-platform-cloud-environment_pia_2022-05.pdf Though supervisory exams focus on the institution, not individual consumers, the CFPB may need limited access to consumer personally identifiable information (PII) to carry out its work.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The majority of PII in SES is collected through examination requests where PII is indirectly part of an entity's response to CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: However, there are situations when the CFPB may directly contact consumers to verify their PII for accuracy and completeness.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB collects and maintains limited PII using SES including: PII about consumers who are past, present, or potential consumers of depository and nondepository entities under the authority of the CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: PII about entity employees who are submitters of the information requested by CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: PII about CFPB employees who are involved in the supervision process.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The type and extent of PII collected depends on the type of examination being conducted.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Information collected through Supervision and Examination activities and maintained in the SES is covered by the following System of Records Notices (SORNs): CFPB.002 - Depository Institution Supervision Database and CFPB.003 - Non-Depository Institution Supervision Database 4 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB conducts this privacy impact assessment (PIA) to document its use of the SES and to identify associated privacy risks and mitigations.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The scope of this PIA is limited to the privacy risks and technical controls associated with the maintenance and use of PII within the SES.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The SES collects data that are related to administrative actions, investigations, and/or audits.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 5 The collected data are not subject to requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The primary risks identified in this PIA are related to the following: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information Individual Participation Data Minimization Security.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The CFPB examination personnel request information, which may include PII, from supervised entities to conduct supervision activities.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: There is a risk that the examination personnel may misuse the PII, or use the PII in a way that is inconsistent with the purpose of collection.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, the CFPB provides training to examination personnel prior to access to PII so they understand their responsibility in collecting, handling, and safeguarding the data.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: CFPB examination personnel must review the relevant policies and engage in other formal and nonformal training forums to learn how the CFPB business process works and how to appropriately use the information that is collected during examinations.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: For example, examination personnel are trained to securely store information pertaining to investigations in Microsoft O365 SharePoint, and not on individual IT system equipment assigned to them.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Additionally, those with access to the SES receive training that includes a briefing on confidentiality before they are granted access to the system.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: This briefing includes a reminder to employees that the PII contained within the system may be subject to the Privacy Act.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Examination personnel are also required to conduct the examinations within a specified scope.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Once the scope of the exam is set, the Examiner in Charge (EIC) works to customize the information requests for a particular entity.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: These requests are approved by senior management before sending to the entity.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: CFPB examination personnel also rely on role-based permissions in the SES to make sure that all information collected is used for its intended purpose.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: PII within the SES may also be shared with other cloud environments for data storage and document collaboration.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: For example, the SES is built on the Salesforce 6 cloud platform and Microsoft 7 0365 facilitates document collaboration and management for SES.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: CFPB's Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment also acts as a staging area for files that have not yet been virusscanned pending transfer to Microsoft O365.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: This presents a risk that PII stored within another cloud environment may be accessed by an unauthorized individual or that a breach within the cloud environment may impact business operations within the SES.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The CFPB mitigates this risk by sharing the SES data only with systems that have achieved an Authority to Operate (ATO) based upon the CFPB A&A processes.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Connections between other cloud environments are assessed by the CFPB to apply role-based environment access controls to ensure the security and privacy of the interconnection.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: Any proposed data sharing between the cloud environments is also assessed to ensure only authorized entities can access data within the SES.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The CFPB also configures security controls at a granular level within each application to prevent sharing of PII externally.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: For example, CFPB disables external sharing within Microsoft O365 SharePoint, prohibiting any linked document from being opened outside the CFPB environment.
sentences.heading: Limits on Uses and Sharing of Information

sentences.text: The PII collected in SES is typically provided by an entity pursuant to applicable laws and regulations, rather than directly by consumers.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: Consumers therefore do not have opportunities to opt out or decline to share PII in this context, and there isa risk that individuals are not aware that their information is collected by CFPB, and that CFPB cannot provide a way for individuals to access records that are submitted by supervised entities.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: However, given the nature of the information collection, the PII included in the SES cannot be accessed or amended by the public because allowing access would jeopardize a pending CFPB examination, investigation, or enforcement action.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: This risk is acceptable because the supervision of entities is required by the Dodd-Frank Act, the CFPB needs to request information from entities that may contain PII to sufficiently meet this statutory requirement, and PII in the SES system is not collected for the purpose of analyzing specific consumers.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: 6 See https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_salesforce-platform-cloud-environment_pia_2022-05.pdf 7 See https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_microsoft-cloud-gss_pia_2022-07.pdf Furthermore, CFPB offers a means through the Privacy Act for individuals to access, amend, or correct, their records at their request.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: However, PII in the SES cannot be accessed or changed if doing so would impact the CFPB's ability to supervise an entity or if doing so would harm a pending investigation or enforcement action.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: Information about Privacy Act requests is available in the SES SORNs, CFPB.002 - Depository Institution Supervision Database and CFPB.003 Non-Depository Institution Supervision Database for the SES and at https://www.consumerfinance.gov/foia-requests/.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: There is a risk that documents or other information provided by entities to the CFPB during the examination process may include unnecessary PII about consumers or employees of the entity.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: To help mitigate this risk, the CFPB trains examiners to collect only relevant and necessary information, as well as how to properly handle and protect sensitive, confidential, and personal information.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Examiners must complete the confidentiality and privacy briefing when they initially onboard and on an annual basis thereafter.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Where practicable, the CFPB uses de-identified information or information that does not contain name or other direct identifier of the consumer to conduct the examination.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The CFPB works directly with the entities it supervises to limit the amount of sensitive information shared during the examination process.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: There is a risk that the substantial amounts of information on consumers and their financial transactions in the SES may be a target for hackers, identity thieves, and other cyber threats.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The CFPB mitigates this risk by implementing extensive security controls and safeguards for the SES and the GSS that hosts it to protect the information in the system against unauthorized disclosure and access.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: All employees at CFPB are required to use a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card to log into their device.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: After logging in, examination personnel may log in to the SES utilizing ingle sign on and two factor authentication methods.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Once they attempt to sign in the user is prompted via Okta Verify on their CFPB-provided cellphone to confirm they did make that action.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: This then allows the user into the system.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: There is also a risk that unauthorized individuals may gain access to the information in the SES.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The CFPB mitigates this risk by only granting access to the system to authorized users who, based on their need to know, will be restricted to the minimal amount of PII required or appropriate to carry out their assigned job responsibilities.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Access is terminated or reduced as necessary should the authorized CFPB staff no longer have a need to know the information, change job functions, is terminated, or resigns.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: In addition, the CFPB issues authorized personnel non-transferable usernames to SES as required for fulfilling official duties.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: This access is only issued after employees have completed the system's training seminar, which includes confidentiality and privacy briefings.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Since access to all information included in the SES may not be necessary for all CFPB employees with supervision responsibilities, the system has unique user roles.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: For example, employees who supervise other employees with examination responsibilities may require access to human resources systems associated with scheduling, whereas employees tasked with non-examination duties may not require such access.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The user roles assigned to each employee when they are granted access to the system reflect their individual needs for information in the system.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The CFPB is also aware of the importance of interconnection security.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: As mentioned in previous sections above, the CFPB only shares SES data with systems that have achieved an ATO based upon the CFPB A&A process.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The SES connections with cloud environments are assessed by rolebased environment access controls.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The technical, physical, and administrative controls implemented to promote individual participation, minimization, and accountability are appropriate.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: One of the CFPB's chief responsibilities is supervising entities that provide consumer financial products and services.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: The CFPB communicates with entities responsible for developing, selling, marketing, and administering these products and services, through entity point of contacts responsible for managing the entity and its legal compliance responsibilities.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: During these communications, CFPB examiners may collect PII about the entity employees to the extent necessary to identify them and to facilitate further communications.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: As part of the examination process, CFPB examiners review individual transaction records while determining whether an entity is conducting business in accordance with applicable federal laws.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: Those transaction records can contain PII about consumers who have been offered or who have purchased the products and services being examined.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: The records, including PII, are particularly important if the conclusion is that an entity has not been properly following the law, because in those instances, the CFPB may order the entity to correct its mistakes.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: For example, corrective actions may require identifying consumers whose accounts reflect non-compliance and taking specific steps to remedy the non-compliance.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: Internally, the CFPB may share information from the SES, in the form of reports or through access to the system, with members of the enforcement and fair lending teams 10 .
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: The CFPB only shares information with authorized users through secure channels, such as online portals like Microsoft O365 SharePoint or through encrypted email, and only with individuals what are authorized to review the reports.
sentences.heading: 2. Describe CFPB's objective for the information.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the Act), Public Law No. 111-203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB administers, enforces, and implements federal consumer financial protection laws, and, among other powers, has authority to protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, and abusive practices when obtaining consumer financial products or services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB receives complaints, inquiries, and feedback about consumer financial products, services, and the entities providing them.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One of the primary functions of the CFPB under the Dodd-Frank Act is collecting, investigating, and responding to consumer complaints.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 The CFPB is also tasked with analyzing complaints to identify trends in service delivery to consumers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To fulfill these obligations, the CFPB created the Office of Consumer Response (Consumer Response) to answer consumers' questions, handle consumers' complaints, and analyze and share complaint data and insights.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer Response engages directly with consumers to understand the challenges they face in the financial marketplace and responds to their inquiries about consumer financial products and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer Response accepts complaints about financial products and services from consumers via the CFPB's website, www.ConsumerFinance.gov/complaint/, by phone, and physical mail.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addition, the CFPB accepts complaints by referral from other government agencies, the White House, and Congressional offices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addressing a complaint or inquiry, Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the CFPB for further administrative action.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The consumer complaints or inquiries themselves (including records about the complaint, details and supporting documents) are collected by Consumer Response and maintained in the Consumer Response System (CRS), which is the CFPB system of record for these interactions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform 2 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 Consumer complaints are submissions that express dissatisfaction with, or communicate suspicion of wrongful conduct by, an identifiable entity related to a consumer's personal experience with a financial product or service.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 2 For more information, see the Consumer Response Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) and Salesforce Platform (Cloud Environment) PIA on the CFPB website: www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/privacy-impact-assessments.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB continually strives to protect sensitive complaint information from disclosure, while also making certain non-sensitive complaint data, which is collected as part of its complaint function, available to the public.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One way the CFPB currently accomplishes this is by sharing de-identified individual-level complaint data with the public through the Consumer Complaint Database (or the Database).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Database, established pursuant to Sections 1012, 1013, 1016, 1021, 1022, and 1034 of the Act, was launched on June 19, 2012. It was initially only populated with credit card complaint data but has since expanded to include complaint data about mortgages, bank accounts and services, student loans, vehicle and other consumer loans, credit reporting, money transfers, debt collection, payday loans, and other consumer financial products and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The purpose of the Consumer Complaint Database is to provide consumers with timely and understandable information about consumer financial products and services via the complaints that consumers submit about these financial products and services, and to improve the functioning, transparency, and efficiency of markets for such products and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB discloses data associated with consumer complaints via the Consumer Complaint Database to include consumer complaint narratives and public-facing response categories companies select to categorize their response to each complaint.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB only discloses consumer narratives if it has received specific consent from the consumer to be included via an 'opt-in consumer consent' approach.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: When submitting a complaint, consumers are provided an opportunity to check a consent box giving the CFPB permission to publish the narrative.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The opt-in consent states that: (a) whether or not consent is given will have no impact on how the CFPB handles the complaint, (b) the consumer may withdraw consent at any time and the narrative will be removed from the Consumer Complaint Database, and (c) the CFPB will take reasonable steps to remove personally identifiable information (PII) from the complaint to minimize, but not eliminate, the risk of re-identification.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB performs the following tasks to de-identify, or 'scrub,' PII from complaint narratives following the Consumer Response Scrubbing Standard published on the CFPB's website at www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/data-use.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: At a high level, the CFPB follows a three-step procedure: (1) an automated process, called a script, reviews narrative content and identifies and removes PII; (2) a CFPB staff member then reviews the narrative and removes any additional PII that the script may not have identified and removed, and (3) another script reviews the narrative to ensure that the prior steps have not missed any PII.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Once a narrative successfully completes these steps, the narrative is eligible for publication.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Periodically, CFPB staff perform an additional quality assurance review on narrative content to validate that the automated reviews and CFPB staff review are performed accurately.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Any narratives identified with remaining PII will be reprocessed using the above steps.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: If process issues are identified during quality assurance reviews, then the Consumer Response Scrubbing Standard will be reviewed and corrected, as appropriate.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Whether or not the consumer provides consent to publish their narrative, the related company is given the opportunity to provide an optional public response for inclusion in the Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Within the secure web portal that companies use to respond to the complaints, the CFPB provides a list of public company response options, giving companies the option to recommend a structured public response.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB believes that this approach allows companies sufficient flexibility to assess legal, business, reputational, and other considerations relevant to the decision of whether to provide a public facing response.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The release of narratives provides consumers with additional timely and understandable information about consumer financial products and services and improves the functioning, transparency, and efficiency of markets for such products and services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The release of the complaint narratives facilitates research, review, and analysis of complaint data and provides companies with greater insight into issues and challenges occurring across their markets, which can supplement their own company-specific perspectives and lend more insight into appropriate practices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is updating this Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to discuss the privacy risks and mitigations associated with an updated approach to the scrubbing of the Consumer Response complaint narratives prior to publication.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: As mentioned above, the CFPB documents the collection and use of PII, and the associated privacy risks and mitigations for the Consumer Complaint Database and CRS in separate PIAs, found at: www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/privacy-impact-assessments.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Consumer complaints received by the CFPB are subject to the System of Records Notice (SORN) CFPB.005-Consumer Response System 3 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Pursuant to the Paperwork Reduction Act, the CFPB has received OMB approval under control number 3170-0011 for collections associated with the CFPB's Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The primary privacy risks associated with the Consumer Complaint Database are risks related to: Data Minimization Data Quality and Integrity Individual Participation Security
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: When submitting a complaint, there is a risk that a consumer may disclose more information than necessary for the service they are seeking.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, Consumer Response leverages processes and controls that limit the amount of information that a consumer is required to provide.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Moreover, consumers are discouraged from including personal information in their complaint submission.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: For example, when a consumer submits a complaint through the Consumer Portal via the Consumer Resource Center (CRC), the consumer is reminded to provide only the necessary information to submit and route the complaint.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: For any PII provided with the complaint, the CFPB applies a robust scrubbing standard to remove personal identifiers and other personal information prior to publication in the Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: If any PII remains in a complaint that is published to the Consumer Complaint Database, staff are trained on how to report and handle suspected privacy breaches to mitigate harm to an impacted individual.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: In certain cases, if staff are unable to sufficiently de-identify a narrative, the narrative will not be published.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: For internal users, access to complaint information is limited to staff with a business justification to access PII.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: In some cases-and in compliance with record management requirements to limit the amount of sensitive information held by the CFPB-the CFPB may not collect or will immediately delete certain sensitive information (e.g., account numbers) that a consumer provided to CRC systems, if it is not needed for that service.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Prior to release in the database, Consumer Response scrubs and reviews each complaint to remove PII from the complaint.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: The complaint is also reviewed to ensure that the scrubbed complaint retains the basis of the complaint and to ensure the quality and integrity of the unstructured complaint narrative.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: The commercial relationship between the company and the consumer and their authorized representative is verified before disclosing it in the Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: The CFPB only forwards complaints to companies when they contain the required fields, including the complaint narrative, the consumer's requested resolution, and the consumer's contact information.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: Within the secure web portal that companies use to respond to complaints, the CFPB has added a set list of company responses, giving companies the ability to recommend a public-facing response addressing the substance of the consumer's complaint (e.g., Company has responded to the consumer and the CFPB and chooses not to provide a public response, Company disputes the facts presented in the complaint).
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: Companies are under no obligation to provide this publicfacing response.
sentences.heading: Data Quality and Integrity

sentences.text: Every consumer who submits a complaint on the website is provided an option to consent to the release of their narrative in the Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: The CFPB does not intend to release a narrative until the consumer expressly consents to publication and the CFPB has determined that the narrative has been de-identified according to a robust scrubbing standard.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: If the consumer changes their mind, they can withdraw consent at any time and, when the database is updated, the consumer's information is removed from the Consumer Complaint Database.
sentences.heading: Individual Participation

sentences.text: The complaint narratives are transferred from the CRS to a CFPB system where PII is scrubbed from the narrative content.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: After the narratives have been scrubbed, they are put back into the CRS.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: There is a risk that transferring the data between the systems could create a vulnerability in the security of the system, allowing a bad actor to access the complaint data containing PII.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: The CFPB has mitigated this risk by deploying an interconnection security agreement (ISA) between these systems to implement logical and physical access controls that limit data access only to authorized CFPB users.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: For example, the data are protected by a firewall cluster and load balancers and a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) device monitors unusual and/or malicious network activity.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: When such activity is detected, logs are reviewed by the CFPB's Cybersecurity Team for investigation and further action as appropriate.
