sentences.text: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) Office of Enforcement (Enforcement) maintains a team of eDiscovery professionals to manage the discovery process in litigation and investigations.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Discovery is the process of identifying, preserving, collecting, reviewing, analyzing, and producing information during an investigation or during administrative or civil actions. eDiscovery is simply the extension of this well-established process to the ElectronicallyStored Information (ESI) that an organization might possess, including email, instant, messages, word processing files, spreadsheets, presentations, social networking content, voice and audio recordings, content stored in databases or collaboration systems, and all the devices on which this information might be stored.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Professional litigation support products/tools and services help to support several functions related to investigation and litigation.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: These tools and services enable the litigator to control and manage much larger volumes of case materials, and much more complex information, much more quickly, and to much greater effect, than would otherwise be possible.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: For example, these tools ingest, analyze, process, format, and organize bureau records for search, retrieval, review, correlation, flagging, and presentation in various data formats (e.g., Microsoft Word and Microsoft Excel), allowing document analysis in bulk within a single data file.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats and identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process. eDiscovery tools provide redaction capabilities which allows for and automates the identification of protected information (e.g., personally identifiable information) by searching for names, phrases, and terms (collectively, 'keywords') that are input by the reviewing attorney.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: This allows the reviewing attorney to customize keywords for each set of documents or cases that may indicate the existence of privileged or protected information.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: The tool uses that information to automatically flag files that contain those keywords for the attorney, who will review and determine if the files or information therein should be protected from disclosure.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: In addition, Enforcement requires the capability to forensically collect data from external entities when immediate access is granted by a court, often in conjunction with a Temporary Restraining Order. eDiscovery tools allow CFPB Staff 1 to forensically extract data from storage media to use as evidence in legal proceedings and to gather and store information in a secure and forensically sound manner, including electronic and non-electronic (e.g., paper) information.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Early case assessment tools are used in conjunction with other tools to process forensically collected data to identify the types of data collected and conduct triage on a large quantity of information to determine what must be reviewed.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Finally, other tools provide trial and investigative hearing support.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: These events require the use of various specialized trial presentation software tools, which display exhibits, either during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: The CFPB employs the Legal Technology Support Team (LTST), which hosts and provides Enforcement with a suite of eDiscovery applications and tools to process and manage these legal activities.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: LTST's application suite is comprised of these customized commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) tools and cloud-based solutions (on-premises or vendor-owned) to ensure that CFPB can effectively collect, store, process, transmit, and maintain critical information related to CFPB investigations, litigation, and enforcement processes.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: To supplement CFPB's eDiscovery workload, Enforcement has procured the services of a federal contractor to provide eDiscovery and litigation support services.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: Similarly, these services include a wide range of professional litigation support products/tools and services help to support several functions related to investigation and litigation.
sentences.heading: Background

sentences.text: However, these tools are housed in a contract-owned environment.

sentences.text: There is a risk that CFPB records maintained in the contractor-owned environment will be retained for longer than necessary.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, all CFPB records are transferred electronically to the contractor, except for in rare situations where the original documents are paper-based.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: In these situations, the original documents are shipped to the contractor for scanning and the paper documents are returned to the CFPB.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: CFPB mitigates this risk by implementing a process where all electronic documents maintained within the contractor's environment will either be transferred back to CFPB or destroyed three (3) months after the case-also referred to as a matter-is closed.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Upon closure of a matter, the CFPB the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) notifies the contractor.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The COR receives an automated electronic notification when a matter closes and barring any instructions to retain the records longer (e.g., investigative purposes), the COR will manually notify the contractor three months later.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: The contractor will then provide the COR with the chain of custody and Final Disposition certificate signed and dated.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: Records transferred back to the CFPB will then be maintained in a locked evidence locker and destroyed in accordance with the relevant records retention schedule.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: As noted above, the CFPB retains records in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedules and NARA-approved Bureau record schedules.
sentences.heading: Data Minimization

sentences.text: There is a risk of loss or unauthorized access or use, destruction, modification, or unintended or inappropriate disclosure for information maintained in a contractor-environment.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: This risk is mitigated.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, all CFPB staff, including federal contractors with access to CFPB information and systems are subject to the same federal laws, regulations, and policies while working at the CFPB and proceed through the same background investigations for suitability and security clearance determinations.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Other requirements placed on federal contractors also include those associated with Federal Acquisition Regulations.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Bureau records are only shared with contractors that have a need to know based on job duties.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: CFPB records are transferred to the contractor using encrypted physical media (e.g., hard drives) or over secure File Transfer Protocol and vice versa.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: These records are maintained by the contractor in a FedRAMP-secured environment.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: All users are required to read and sign the 'Employee Rules of Behavior' before being granted access.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Access to the environment is strictly provided through an approval authorization process.
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: In addition, the following access controls are in place to prevent misuse or unauthorized access to CFPB records:
sentences.heading: Security

sentences.text: Assignment of unique account name and complex passwords; Multifactor authentication via PIV; RSA soft tokens are used for second factor authentication (if applicable); Automatic removal of inactive accounts; Least privilege access procedures; and Role-based access controls.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: The contractor employs role-based access controls to ensure that users only have access to the environment and CFPB records maintained therein that are necessary and relevant to their assigned job duties.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: For example, these role-based access controls only permit a user to see or modify information for cases or matters to which they are assigned.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: Finally, the contractor has established oversight controls through robust auditing features to identify and support accountability for unauthorized use/misconduct.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: Suspicious or unauthorized access is monitored and logged, thereby deterring users from inappropriate access and use of CFPB information.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: Information maintained in the audit log includes but is not limited to, the type of audit event, date and time event occurred, and user ID to identify the employee.
sentences.heading: Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024

sentences.text: The audit log is stored separately and protected from viewing or access by authorized users.

sentences.text: Section 1071 of the Consumer Protection Act of 2010, title X of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, Public Law No. 111-203, 124 Stat. 1376, 2004 (2010) amended the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA), 15 U.S.C. 1691 et. seq.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: (hereinafter Section 1071) to require covered financial institutions to collect data regarding applications for credit for women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses and report it to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Section 1071's statutory purposes are to (1) facilitate enforcement of fair lending laws, and (2) enable communities, governmental entities, and creditors to identify business and community development needs and opportunities of women-owned, minorityowned, and small businesses.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Section 1071 specifies data that covered financial institutions are required to collect from small business applicants and report to the CFPB 1 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It also provides authority for the CFPB to require additional data that it determines would fulfill Section 1071's statutory purposes.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Section 1071 further provides that financial institutions may not include the personally identifiable information (PII) of applicants as part of the data collection disclosed to CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Pursuant to ECOA, the CFPB issued the Small Business Lending Rule, codified as subpart B to Regulation B, 12 C.F.R. 1002.101 et seq., which implements the small business lending data collection requirements set forth in Section 1071. Regulation B prescribes rules for covered financial institutions to follow when collecting and compiling data related to small business lending as required by Section 1071. The data that will be collected by covered financial institutions from small business credit applicants includes the type of credit being applied for; the credit purpose; and the amount applied for; census tract based on an address or location provided by the applicant; gross annual revenue for the preceding fiscal year; the 3-digit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the applicant; the number of workers that the applicant has; the applicant's time in business; and the number of principal owners the applicant has.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: 1 See Small Business Lending under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (Regulation B) final rule published here: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/31/2023-07230/small-business-lending-under-the-equalcredit-opportunity-act-regulation-b Moreover, covered financial institutions must collect and report certain demographic information about the applicant and its principal owners.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The demographic data collected will include whether the applicant is a minority-owned, women-owned or LGBTQI+-owned business, and the ethnicity, race, and sex/gender of the applicant's principal owners.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Finally, covered financial institutions must report data points that are provided solely by the financial institution.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: For all applications this data includes: a unique identifier for each application for or extension of credit; the application date; the application method (that is, the means by which the applicant submitted the application); the application recipient (that is, whether the financial institution or its affiliate received the application directly, or whether it was received by the financial institution via a third party); the action taken by the financial institution on the application; and the action taken date.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: For denied applications, there is also a data point for denial reasons.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: For applications that are approved, additional data is required including the amount originated or approved, and pricing information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB created the Small Business Lending system (herein referred to as the SBL system) built within CFPB's Amazon Web Services (AWS) 2 environment to collect small business lending data from covered financial institutions, as required by Section 1071. Prior to full deployment of the system, the CFPB is conducting beta-testing activities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: During the beta-testing phase, the CFPB will test the functionalities of the SBL system with volunteer participants from covered financial institutions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: During the beta-testing activities, the volunteer user or point of contact (POC) from covered financial institutions is instructed to only submit fake data through the SBL system; the CFPB is not collecting any real application data during this phase.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB will provide simulated datasets to be used for this purpose.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Any information provided to the CFPB during betatesting will only be used for testing purposes.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is conducting this PIA to document and assess privacy risks associated with the limited collection of PII from the user or POC during the beta testing activities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To access the SBL system for testing, the user or POC must first visit Login.gov, which is owned and operated by the General Services Administration (GSA) 3 to create an account.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The user or POC must provide their full name and email to create an account with Login.gov; their information is then shared with and collected by the SBL system to authenticate the account and grant access to the system.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The user or POC is then directed to the CFPB Regulatory Technology Home web application 4 where they create a User Profile.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The SBL system collects the user's or POC's full name, business email address, phone number, and mailing address, along with other information related to the covered financial institutions, to create the User Profile.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Once the User Profile is created, the participant is able to test the submission capabilities in the SBL system by uploading and providing fake data through the system.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB testing team receives the data and validates that the submission process is functioning correctly.

sentences.text: Nonbank Registry System Privacy Impact Assessment September 2024
The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the Act) 1 established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Act requires the CFPB to monitor markets for consumer financial products and services for risks to consumers to support its various functions and authorizes the CFPB to establish a nonbank registration program.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Pursuant to sections 1022(b) and (c) and 1024(b) of the Act, the CFPB issued the Registry of Nonbank Covered Persons Subject to Certain Agency and Court Orders Final Rule-referred to as the Orders Rule-on June 3, 2024. 2 The Orders Rule generally requires nonbank covered persons (hereinafter referred to as 'nonbanks'), including nonbanks subject to the CFPB's supervisory authority, to register with the CFPB if they meet certain criteria as discussed below.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Generally, 'nonbanks' are companies involved in the offering or provision of consumer financial products or services that are not insured depository institutions or insured credit unions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To facilitate the nonbank registration program, the CFPB Supervision Division (Supervision) developed the Nonbank Registry (NBR) System-also known as the Nonbank Registry or registry-and external-facing portal-known as the Nonbank Registry Portal-to collect, use, and maintain information on nonbanks.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Through the Nonbank Registry Portal, nonbanks are required to register certain final public orders, including consent and stipulated orders and judgments (hereinafter referred to as 'covered orders') 3 obtained or issued by the CFPB or any other government agency (federal, state, tribal, or local) based on the violation of certain consumer financial laws.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Public agency or court orders are legally binding orders intended to prevent and remedy violations of the covered law.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: When an agency issues such an order, or seeks a court order, it typically has determined that the problems at the applicable nonbank are sufficiently serious to merit the expenditure of that agency's limited resources and perhaps the attention of the courts.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Orders Rule only pertains to covered orders that are 'public,' i.e. , that previously have been published by the issuing agency and/or court (or were required to be published by the issuing agency or court).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: To prevent the unnecessary disclosure of information maintained in covered orders, covered nonbanks are instructed in the Orders Rule to redact any nonpublic portions of the covered orders before submitting them to the registry.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Additionally, the Orders Rule requires certain registered nonbanks subject to the CFPB's supervisory authority to submit on an annual basis a written statement signed by a senior executive (hereinafter referred to as 'attesting executive' or 'executive') with respect to the nonbank's compliance with the covered order during the preceding calendar year.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The statement will generally describe the steps undertaken by the executive to review and oversee the nonbank's activities subject to the applicable covered order for the preceding calendar year.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The executive will also provide a written, signed attestation regarding the nonbank's compliance with the covered order.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The collection of this information allows the CFPB to prioritize supervision resources, assists in supervisory and examination activities ( e.g. , potentially increasing supervisory effort related to some repeat offenders), improves accountability, and deters misconduct among nonbanks.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Finally, the Orders Rule allows the CFPB to publish some of the information collected from nonbanks for use by members of the public as well as other regulatory agencies.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: As stated in the Orders Rule, Congress authorized the CFPB to share its insights gained as the result of its market monitoring duties with a wider audience and granted the CFPB the authority to make nonconfidential information available to the public 'as is in the public interest.' 4 However, publication is not mandatory.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Therefore, the CFPB has sole discretion in determining whether to publish certain information maintained in the NBR System and the format of publication designed to protect confidential information in accordance with the Orders Rule.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act 1 established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: A central part of the Bureau's mission is to protect consumers and make sure they are treated fairly in the financial marketplace.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One way the CFPB does this is by enforcing federal consumer financial laws and holding financial service providers accountable for their actions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Pursuant to sections 1052, 1053, and 1054 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. § 5562-5564 2 the CFPB's Enforcement Division (Enforcement) is authorized to conduct investigations, issue civil investigation demands, initiate administrative adjudications, and initiate public enforcement actions in state and federal court against persons 3 (hereinafter referred to as 'entities and individuals') for engaging in conduct that may violate rules and/or statutes within the CFPB's authority.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB also coordinates with other federal or state agencies (e.g., Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Department of Justice, and state Attorneys General) to inform related work and reduce the burden on institutions that are the subject of an enforcement investigation.

sentences.text: 3 The rules governing enforcement investigations under section 1052 of the Dodd-Frank Act, 12 U.S.C. § 5562, apply to a "person" as defined in 12 C.F.R. Part 1080.This term encompasses individuals as well as partnerships, companies, corporations, associations (incorporated or unincorporated), trusts, estates, cooperative organizations, or other entities, as specified in 12 C.F.R. § 1080.2. In contrast, 'individuals', as defined under the Privacy Act of 1974, are typically U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents.

sentences.text: This definition does not extend to an entity that is not a natural person, such as partnerships, companies, corporations, associations (whether incorporated or unincorporated), trusts, estates, or cooperative organizations.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: However, non-natural entities such as corporations are considered legal 'persons' and can be held liable similarly to individuals.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Therefore, they may also be identified in an enforcement investigation and held liable for consumer financial law violations.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Additionally, the Bureau's ability to enforce the Consumer Financial Protection Act (CFPA), including its prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts and practices, is limited to 'covered persons' and 'service providers.' 12 U.S.C. §§ 5531(a), 5536. 'Covered person' includes 'any person that engages in offering or providing a consumer financial product or service.' 'Service provider' includes 'any person that provides a material service to a covered person in connection with the offering or provision by such covered person of a consumer financial product or service.' The CFPA also extends to persons who 'knowingly or recklessly provide substantial assistance.' Other federal consumer financial laws are broader and apply to 'any person,' subject only to the limitations in Subtitle B of the CFPA.

sentences.text: The original Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for the Enforcement Matter Management System-previously known as the Matter Management System PIA-was published on May 24, 2012, was updated on October 22, 2012, and again on October 22, 2024. sentences.text: In assessing whether to open an investigation, Enforcement weighs a number of factors, including, but not limited to, whether: There is a plausible set of facts that, if proven, would amount to a violation of one or more federal consumer financial laws; There is reason to believe that one or more specific entities may be engaging in the conduct described in those facts; There is evidence of a magnitude of harm that justifies investment of resources; There are sufficient resources available to properly address the matter; and The devotion of those resources is consistent with the strategic planning and articulated priorities or warrants a conscious departure from those plans and priorities.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, Public Law No. 111-203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau).

sentences.text: The CFPB is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.

sentences.text: The Geographic Information System (GIS) technology provides the CFPB with a geospatial data, analytics, geocoding, and mapping software tool to support analysis conducted by CFPB program, including the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) program, the Small Business Lending (SBL) program, the Division of Research, Monitoring, and Regulation (RMR), the Supervision Division (SUP), and Enforcement Division (ENF) 1 .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB's use of GIS technology is authorized by Section 1021(c)(6) of the Dodd-Frank Act, 2 which authorizes the CFPB to perform such support activities as may be necessary or useful to facilitate other functions of the Bureau.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB's GIS technology provides the following capabilities and functionalities: Mapping and visualization: allows CFPB users to use an address/location data to visualize data spatially on a map and share those visualizations to help improve business decisions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Increasing efficiency: allows concurrent use of geocoding and geolocation capabilities.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Analytics: provides advanced analytics tools to help users identify patterns, trends, and anomalies in their data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Data management: GIS tools have their own data store and allow authorized users to connect to other existing data stores and leverage ready-to-use storage, such as those hosted within CFPB's Amazon Web Services (AWS) Alto environment.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Security: provides a secure, browser-based enterprise system that allows users to control, store, and access data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Authentication: allows user management and authentication with Single Sign-On (SSO).
sentences.heading: Overview

Overview

sentences.text: The data used by the GIS technology includes information, including personally identifiable information (PII), previously collected by CFPB programs such as location of loans (e.g., home or business address), loan application/borrower information, bank branch locations, address of loan applications, and analysis of trends and actions associated with type of loans, along with publicly available location data, such as Census data or other official data mapping layers that are used as a resource and standard data for various programs performing spatial analysis.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CFPB-employed GIS technology stack has three components: desktop software, online/public portals, and an Enterprise deployment for managing and controlling GIS product use within the organization.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: GIS users load data into and conduct analysis in the desktop software.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It allows users to conduct analysis, create visualizations, and manage geospatial data for a variety of uses at the CFPB.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The online portal is solely used for license/entitlement administration by the geospatial administrators.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Enterprise deployment is comprised of various components: the Enterprise Server powers mapping and analysis; the Enterprise Portal is a central internal hub where users can create, share, and manage maps, apps, and spatial data and share with internal collaborators; the Enterprise Data Store provides data storage; and the Enterprise Web Adaptor integrates the server and portal with CFPB infrastructure.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Enterprise technology allows a greater number of users to access the GIS software and utilize geocoding services concurrently without license restrictions.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The online instance of the GIS tool is FedRAMP Moderate certified and provided through Amazon Web Services (AWS).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Currently the CFPB uses only the desktop software with a limited use of the online/public portals for license management.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: As part of this Enterprise deployment, the CFPB will enable the GIS Enterprise technology mentioned above.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The online component will be integrated in the future for specific use cases and will be documented in separate privacy impact assessment (PIA) appendices or updates.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Office of Regulation Technology (RegTech), which manages the HMDA and SBL programs, remains current on state-of-the-art technology that supports fair, competitive, and transparent consumer financial market.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: As such, RegTech owns and manages the GIS technology for Bureauwide use; however, other CFPB offices with a need to know are granted access to the technology and the resource data stored on the server, such as the publicly available Census data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: While PII such as home addresses may be entered into the GIS technology to gather information related to a geographic location, the GIS technology is not used by CFPB to retrieve records about individuals (e.g., homeowners); therefore, it is not a system of records.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The data used by the GIS technology may be sourced from a Privacy Act of 1974 covered system of record.

sentences.text: 2.1 Explain how the CFPB only collects and maintains the information, that is directly relevant and necessary to accomplish the specified purpose(s).
sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: The GIS technology is limited in the type of data they process and analyze.
sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: The technology is designed to leverage location data to produce trends, mapping, visualizations, and analyses.
sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: As noted above, the information collected by the system may include information that is not location based such as demographic information, income, and loan amounts.
sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: 2. Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: Privacy Risk : There is a risk that information maintained in the GIS technology may be retained longer than necessary to accomplish the purpose for which it was originally collected.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: Mitigation : Data used within the GIS technology is considered transitory.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: Program specific record schedules outline the retention period for the data used for input and the resulting output.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: This risk is further mitigated by documented internal processes that require the deletion of PII and/or sensitive intermediate data within one week after the final output is processed.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: Mitigation : To mitigate this risk, the CFPB has established technical controls and privacy safeguards to ensure only a limited amount of information is entered into the GIS technology.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: For instance, users are provided a guidance document that covers the principle of using the least amount of data required for analysis.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Limits on Information Collection and Retention

sentences.text: It only leverages the data already collected by various CFPB programs which allows program offices to be deliberate about the inputs needed to obtain the desired output.

sentences.text: The GIS technology is a geospatial data management, analytics, research, geocoding, and mapping software tool.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: The CFPB uses the GIS technology to support several primary business lines, and below are examples of how the technology is used: In RegTech, HMDA Ops, RMR, SUP, and Fair Lending the technology is used to support prioritization of examinations.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: For example, the technology may be used to geocode the addresses of loan applications, to identify the location/census tract of a particular applicant for fair lending examination analysis, or as an input to the prioritization process.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: It is also used to conduct spatial analyses, such as cluster analyses or interpolation.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: In ENF, in addition to the geocoding and spatial analyses mentioned above, the technology is used to display relevant case data (e.g., loan location, bank branch locations, census tracts with demographic indicators, etc.) on a map to present during trials.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: In RMR, the technology is used to better understand the distribution of spatial phenomena (e.g., mapping clusters of borrowers across a city, creating weather maps of high and low-interest rate areas, overlaying Census or other maps over our data for additional analyses, calculating the effects of flood risk on mortgage prices, etc.).
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: GIS tasks are also performed across other divisions and offices such as the Office of Technology and Innovation and Consumer Response.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: The technology allows maps to be presented in a static PDF format and as interactive web-maps and web-apps that can be accessed internally by the staff involved, as well as published for the public where it is appropriate or legally required.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: Data can be uploaded into the GIS technology and geocoded so that further analysis can be performed.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: Alternatively, authorized users can leverage pre-geocoded data and intersect those points with additional information such as census tract, population, and other demographics.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: The geocoded output takes the form of either a csv file or map that is further analyzed for programspecific purposes once transferred to the respective server.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Describe the purpose of the information and how the CFPB uses it.

sentences.text: Access to data that is geocoded by the GIS technology, such as HMDA data, may be granted to Bureau users who request it and have a business purpose or need to know.

sentences.text: This internal sharing eliminates the hours of work needed to geocode data for analysis.

sentences.text: However, a user can request an administrator to add an additional user to a private folder for collaborative purpose.

sentences.text: Additionally, the Enterprise instance allows for multiple-user groups where information can be shared within a team or across the Bureau.
sentences.heading: 3.2 Is  the  information  used  or  shared  with  other  CFPB  programs, systems, or projects?

sentences.text: Authorized GIS users are comprised of Bureau employees and contractors.
sentences.heading: 3.2 Is  the  information  used  or  shared  with  other  CFPB  programs, systems, or projects?

sentences.text: Privacy Risk : There is a risk that information may be shared with individuals who do not have a need to know and used in a manner that is inconsistent with the purpose for which it was originally collected.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis: Related to Uses of Information

sentences.text: Mitigation : This risk is mitigated by users having restricted access to certain data sets.

sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: The Privacy Impact Assessment, or 'PIA', provides the public with information about the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's ('CFPB') collection and use of personally identifiable information ('PII').
sentences.heading: Document purpose

sentences.text: PII is any information 'that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity' 1 like a name, address, Social Security number, or place and date of birth.
sentences.heading: Document purpose

sentences.text: The CFPB uses PIAs to document that the PII it collects is used, secured, and destroyed in a way that protects each individual's privacy.
sentences.heading: Document purpose

sentences.text: Each PIA is broken out into sections that reflect the CFPB's Privacy Principles.
sentences.heading: Document purpose

sentences.text: The CFPB's Privacy Principles are a set of nine rules the CFPB follows when it collects or uses PII.
sentences.heading: Document purpose

sentences.text: Directory database
sentences.heading: PROJECT / SYSTEM NAME:

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act ('Act'), Public Law No. 111-203, Title X, established the CFPB.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: The CFPB administers, enforces, and implements federal consumer financial protection laws, and, among other powers, has authority to protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, and abusive practices when obtaining consumer financial products or services.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: 1 Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum 07-16, Safeguarding Against and Responding to the Breach of Personally Identifiable Information, May 22, 2007, (OMB M-07-16) defines PII as information which can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, such as his or her name, social security number, biometric records, etc., alone, or when combined with other personal or identifying information which is linked or linkable to a specific individual, such as date and place of birth, mother's maiden name, etc.' The CFPB built the Directory Database as a single, agency-wide repository of identifying, contact, and registration information about organizations under the Bureau's authority.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: The Directory Database will ensure consistent information across the agency and allow the CFPB to carry out its supervisory, enforcement, and regulatory authorities in an efficient and effective manner.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: Information in the Directory Database is acquired from a variety of sources.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: Once collected , the information is formatted into a standardized form that is used for all similar data across the Bureau.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: Formatting the data for standardization allows for: The information to be accepted and understood by a wider audience within the Bureau; Faster incorporation of new information into the Directory Database and related systems; A reduction in the amount of information (and the space needed to store it) by eliminating redundant information or information that is only different in style; Staff to spend more time working on other duties rather that searching for or formatting information for comparison or reference; and An increase in the quality of decision making because information is valid and reliable.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: Information that is standardized and available in the Directory Database is then 'tagged' in such a way as to track its source (where it came from), as well as the other CFPB systems the information belongs in, and which CFPB employees have a need-to-know the information in the performance of their job functions.
sentences.heading: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES:

sentences.text: The Directory Database includes PII about employees or others associated with institutions under the authority of the CFPB, including: Individuals who own or control organizations that offer or provide consumer financial products or services; Current and former directors, officers, employees, shareholders, agents, and independent contractors of such organizations; Other related persons, as necessary, including, but not limited to, persons who have personal financial arrangements with those described above or serve as representatives or counsel of those described; and Individuals who provide information on those described above or organizations as described above, such as employees of the state attorneys general.

sentences.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act ('Act'), Public Law No. 111203, Title X, established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ('CFPB' or 'Bureau').

sentences.text: The CFPB administers, enforces, and implements federal consumer financial protection laws, and, among other powers, has the authority to protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, and abusive acts and practices when obtaining consumer financial products or services.

sentences.text: The CFPB uses a variety of tools, including our website, www.consumerfinance.gov (ConsumerFinance.gov) to interact with the public.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Use Limitation: The CFPB's website privacy policy describes the information collected from and about visitors to the website and serves as notice about how we plan to use and share the personal information we collect.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The Bureau limits collection of personal information to that which is needed to meet the visitors' requested use of the website.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: How visitors choose to use (or not use) the site's features will determine how much and what information is collected.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The Bureau's updated website privacy policy also details the use of persistent cookies by Google Analytics.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Google Analytics uses persistent cookies for the collection of web metrics and to track visitor interactions; however, the Bureau does not use persistent cookies to collect any PII about visitors to the consumerfinance.gov webpage.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Traffic statistics for the website are only reported to the Bureau anonymously and in the aggregate, and no information provided by Google Analytics is traceable to any specific individual.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: CFPB may share web analytics data with other federal agencies as part of the GSA Digital Analytics Program or the public in aggregate form.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: For example, the CFPB may want and need to share the number of users that have visited consumerfinance.gov in the past six months or how many users utilize a particular tool.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: CFPB may share website analytical data with external organizations or the public, but this will only include aggregated data and the CFPB will never share PII.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Data Quality and Integrity: The Bureau does not verify information that visitors provide to ConsumerFinance.gov, so there is a risk that the information submitted may be erroneous, fraudulent, incomplete, or inaccurate.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Information submitted to the Bureau may be corrected or updated for email lists, blogs, and other contact mediums.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Given the low sensitivity of information collected through the site, and that information collected is for the very specific purpose of meeting the visitor's requested use of the site, this risk is acceptable.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The Bureau is not responsible for the quality of data collected by Google Analytics and used to provide the Bureau with aggregate information.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Security: Visitors to the website choose which information to share with the Bureau or the public through ConsumerFinance.gov. Some of the information is provided for public consumption (e.g. comments), or is of a very-low level of sensitivity (e.g. email addresses).
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The CFPB does not believe that ConsumerFinance.gov is a particularly high risk target.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: However there is a risk that the site could inadvertently disclose some personal information included in comments made by visitors to the site.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The CFPB has mitigated this risk by providing a clear and concise moderation policy, which can be found at http://www.consumerfinance.gov/comment-policy, on ConsumerFinance.gov that outlines what is and is not acceptable information to include in comments and a disclaimer that we reserve the right to remove posts if they are deemed inappropriate or a risk to personal privacy.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: Individual Participation : Since visitors choose how to interact with ConsumerFinance.gov, there are no identifiable risks to individual participation associated with ConsumerFinance.gov. There is, however, a risk that after providing information to ConsumerFinance.gov, the visitor may be limited in ability to add to, delete, or otherwise modify certain information.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: For instance, comments, once posted, may not be able to be removed or edited.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: The Bureau has taken steps to mitigate this risk by providing its moderation policy on ConsumerFinance.gov. The technical, physical, and administrative controls implemented to promote individual participation, minimization, and accountability are appropriate.
sentences.heading: Privacy Risk Analysis

sentences.text: To accomplish its mission the GSA Office it supports must, in the course of business operations, collect personally identifiable information (PII) about the people who use such products and services.
sentences.heading: Document Purpose

sentences.text: PII is any information [1] that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity like a name, address, or place and date of birth.
sentences.heading: Document Purpose

sentences.text: GSA uses Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) to explain how it collects, maintains, disseminates, uses, secures, and destroys information in ways that protect privacy.
sentences.heading: Document Purpose

sentences.text: This PIA comprises sections that reflect GSA's privacy policy and program goals.
sentences.heading: Document Purpose

sentences.text: The sections also align to the Fair Information Practice Principles (FIPPs), a set of eight precepts codified in the Privacy Act of 1974.[2] [1]OMB Memorandum Preparing for and Responding to the Breach of Personally Identifiable Information (OMB M-17-12) defines PII as: 'information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual.' The memorandum notes that 'because there are many different types of information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, the term PII is necessarily broad.' [2] Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552a, as amended.

sentences.text: A: System, Application, or Project Name: GSAFleet.gov B: System, application, or project includes information about: GSA Fleet provides safe, reliable, low-cost vehicle solutions for federal agencies and eligible entities.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: GSA Fleet's suite of offerings include vehicle purchasing, vehicle leasing, and short-term rentals.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: GSAFleet.Gov includes the following components also known as Fleet products: Catalog Store Vehicle Management Services Maintenance and Repair Vehicle Marketplace Progressive Web Application Business Management Below is a description of each component: Catalog - The Catalog maintains all contracts with vendors across the entire GSAFleet.gov. The Catalog contains all the information for new, configurable vehicles and equipment to support customer missions, across all of the Fleet offerings - purchasing, leasing, and rental - and to configure specialty vehicles.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Store - The Store provides the functionality for GSA Fleet customers to research different types of vehicles and equipment, compare one vehicle to another, and compare prices across offerings (purchasing, leasing, short-term rentals), in order to determine the best vehicle or fleet to meet the needs of their agency.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Vehicle Management Services (VMS) - The VMS product provides support to GSA Fleet customers with their Fleet and Motor Pool needs.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: VMS also provides proactive communications to GSA Fleet customers.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: These communications support the use of the vehicle, and ensure that vehicles are safe and compliant.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Maintenance and Repair (M&R) - The M&R product is the first point-of-contact for GSA Fleet customers for any maintenance needs that arise during the use of the vehicles, whether it is for regular preventative maintenance, non-routine mechanical failure, or even vehicle breakdown.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: M&R works with the customer and vendor to document the specific repairs needed, and approve the repairs, to ensure the vehicles are safe and reliable for the customer.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Vehicle Marketplace - The Vehicle Marketplace product is responsible for ensuring that GSA Fleet vehicles that have finished their assignments and will not be reassigned to another Agency, are ready for sale.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Once the vehicle is ready for sale, Vehicle Marketplace uses multiple avenues for the sale of the vehicle.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: The Vehicle Marketplace coordinates with the marshaling vendors (that are managed by the Store) and the transportation vendors to receive the vehicles from GSA Fleet customers and to deliver the vehicles to the auction houses for sale.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: Progressive Web Application - PWAs take a web app and use native features such as service workers or manifests to provide a 'Native' experience for the end users.Business Management - Business Management Product provides oversight into other GSAFleet.gov Products to ensure GSA Fleet Products provide and portray data accurately and consistently to our customers and stakeholders.
sentences.heading: PIA Overview

sentences.text: They also help set rates and pricing, forecasting and budgeting, and provide analysis and recommendations to each of the other products in the GSAFleet.gov. sentences.text: Each year, OLA receives hundreds of inquiries from congressional staffers on behalf of their congressional office or someone in their district.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The system is comprised of two components: OLA Tracking is used to manage the entire lifecycle of the inquiries, and CS Portal is a secure web interface where congressional staffers can submit the inquiries and other messages to the Office of Personnel Management.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This is a replacement to an older system that was decommissioned in November 2023. The new system uses a cloud-version of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The system collects personally identifiable information as part of regular OLA business processes.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: OPM Office of Legislative Affairs (OLA) Constituent Services (CS) handles inquiries from congressional staffers (staffers) asked on behalf of their congressperson or constituents.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These constituents are often annuitants, survivor annuitants, or current or former federal employees.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The inquiries are often about retirement, health care, or other OPM programs and policies.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: OLA CS uses the OLA Tracking & CS Portal system to log the inquiries from staffers, route the inquiries to the appropriate OPM program offices for action, track when and how OPM responded to the staffers, and create reports about that work.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CS Portal is a secure web interface that staffers can use to submit inquiries and associated documents, track the status of that inquiry, and send messages and documents about that inquiry to OLA CS staff.

sentences.text: No data or files are retained or stored in the CS Portal.

sentences.text: The purpose of the Research and Oversight Repository (ROVR) is to assist the Office of Personnel Management's (OPM) Healthcare and Insurance office (HI) to oversee, manage, and analyze the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program and the Postal Service Health Benefits (PSHB) Program by being a repository for enrollee data.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The term 'service use and cost data' includes, but is not limited to, medical claims data, pharmacy claims data, encounter data, and provider data.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted because ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program (e.g., annuitants who suspended their FEHB or PSHB coverage).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The former system name for ROVR was the Health Insurance Data Warehouse (HIDW).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This PIA replaces the HIDW PIA dated July 2, 2021.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The FEHB Program, which includes the PSHB Program 1 , provides health insurance benefits to approximately 8.3 million federal employees, U.S. Postal Service employees and their eligible family members, as well as certain Tribal employees and their eligible family members.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: One of the primary functions of ROVR is to establish and maintain a comprehensive and authoritative FEHB enrollment database, the Master Enrollment Index (MEI), which OPM uses to help administer and manage the FEHB Program to ensure the best value for enrollees and taxpayers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The MEI consists of FEHB enrollees and family members, and those eligible but not enrolled (e.g., annuitants who suspended their FEHB coverage).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Establishment of the enrollment repository promotes effective FEHB Program management and improves program integrity.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Uses of the data include, but are not limited to: 1 The Postal Service Reform Act of 2022 (PSRA) added new section 8903c to Chapter 89 of title 5, United States Code.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The statute directs OPM to establish the Postal Service Health Benefits (PSHB) Program as a new, separate program within the FEHB Program.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Beginning in 2025, Postal Service employees, Postal Service annuitants, and their eligible family members now obtain health benefits coverage through PSHB plans.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Throughout this PIA, references to the 'FEHB Program' or 'FEHB' will include the 'PSHB Program' or 'PSHB,' as relevant.

sentences.text: The completion of USDA Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) is mandated for any rulemaking, program, system, or practice that collects or uses PII under the authority of the E-government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. § 208(b)) and USDA DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

The PIA is designed to identify risk associated with the use of PII by a system, program, project or practice, and to ensure that vital data stewardship issues are addressed for all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) of IT systems.
It also ensures that security and privacy protections are built into an IT system during its development cycle.

By regularly assessing privacy concerns during the development process, USDA ensures that proponents of a program or technology have taken its potential privacy impact into account from the beginning.
The PIA also serves to help identify what level of security risk is associated with a program or technology.
In turn, this allows the Department to properly manage the security requirements under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA).
USDA DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Please note that the E-government Act of 2002 requires that a PIA be made available to the public.
In order to comply with this requirement , PIAs will be published online for the general public to view.

When completing this document please use simple, straight-forward language, avoid overly technical terminology, and write out acronyms the first time you use them to ensure that the document can be read and understood by the general public.
Guidance on how to complete the following PIA Questionnaire is available here.

sentences.text: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) receives thousands of pieces of correspondence and documents and is implementing a new platform called AgWrite, a modernized content management system managed by the USDA Office of Executive Secretariat (OES).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The new system will implement advanced technology to transform how correspondence is processed in OES, supporting standardized processes and role-based access.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted to ensure that personally identifiable information (PII) voluntarily provided by public individuals and organizations is properly safeguarded and controlled while being handled and managed in the system.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: AgWrite is a content management (CMS) system owned and managed by the Office of the Executive Secretariat (OES).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: AgWrite is being leveraged to provide standardized processes and role-based controls to support the receipt and processing of correspondence and other artifacts that require ingestion, review, and approval by business units across USDA.

sentences.text: This PIA is for the Civil Rights Enterprise System (CRES).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: It is a Web-based enterprise-wide suite of applications supporting USDA and all Departmental Agencies by tracking, processing, and managing employment, and program complaints, as well as meeting regulatory reporting requirements.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The PIA is being conducted to maintain ATO.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: CRES is a major application-an enterprise system sponsored by the USDA Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It is a Web-based enterprise-wide suite of applications supporting USDA and all Departmental Agencies by tracking, processing, and managing employment, and program complaints, as well as meeting regulatory reporting requirements.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The system provides core support for the mission of Civil Rights (CR) offices both at the Departmental and Agency levels, and it serves management needs of Agency Heads who by law are charged with the responsibility for Agency compliance with Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and CR.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The initiative encompasses Employment Complaint Processing and Reporting and Program Complaint Processing and Reporting.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addition to the complaint processing CRES also handles Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) which is offered prior to making a complaint, both a formal and informal process .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CRES is a server based application that users connect to via their web browser application.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: There is no client side portion of software that must be installed.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CRES itself is a COTS package of software called iComplaints.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: CRES is co-located at MicroPact Engineering, Inc. MicroPact Engineering provides system, network, development, and administrative security under contract with The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Other than the Internet, CRES has no interconnections or information sharing with other systems.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is for the USDA, Departmental Management (DM) Office of Operations (OO) Operating System for Customer Access and Requests (OSCAR) System.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The DM-OO OSCAR system provides a web-based tool that enables and support multiple business processes across the Office of Operations.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This PIA is being conducted to determine the potential impact of data collected via DM-OO OSCAR.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: DM-OO OSCAR supports multiple business processes across the Office of Operations, including:  Hotline 2.0, a service desk accepting work orders and service requests from USDA employees.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It handles the routing and is the clearing house for all activities through (Washington Area Service Center) WASC.  Waste Management handles the disposal of recyclable and non-recyclable items.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Recycled waste is collected through various methods throughout the facility.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: They include hallway containers cafeteria receptacles and office recycle bins.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Waste is collected and weighed by the janitorial staff.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Record on a form and tuned into the WASC for system entry.  OO Facility Management Division is responsible for generating equipment PM (Periodic Maintenance) requests at an assigned frequency.  Executive Limousine Service provides dispatch limousine service to USDA executives.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It is also responsible for recording maintenance requests for vehicles.  Minor Repairs System processes work order requests for tickets that cost between $500 and $25,000.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It will also track the total costs (such as labor and material) costs for work order tickets below $500.  Project Management module will combine 3 different modules in the current system: Maintenance Control System, Building Project Management, and Repairs and Alteration.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These will become 3 different project types in the new system.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The processes for this module will vary by project type.  Building Permit Management center handles requests for building permits.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: An application for a request is submitted by a customer, which is routed through a process where various reviewers across different disciplines can be assigned to approve the request.  Mechanical Equipment module currently holds information about various equipment; such as water heater, pump, chiller, and (Air Handling Unit) (AHU).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: ePACS collects information required to control physical access to USDA managed facilities and restricted areas within those facilities in all regions across the United States. ePACS maintains individuals' personal individual verification (PIV) information to support the USDA's eff orts related to protecting USDA facilities which includes the USDA Washington DC Visitor Management System (VMS). ePACS provides a centralized infrastructure for the use of the USDA standard identification card (LincPass) for access to federally controlled facilities as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD) - 12. ePACS provides a means for USDA Agencies to deploy electronic access control to its facilities; supports the mitigation of identified threats and vulnerabilities; and ensures that unauthorized individuals do not have access to critical USDA assets.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Incorporated into ePACS is the VMS which allows visitors to respond to meeting invites and registrar to visit USDA locations in Washington, D.C. ePACS utilizes the Lenel OnGuard and Certipath for the trusted visitor software, commercial off the shelf software/client server application. ePACS provides the centralized infrastructure for utilization of the USDA standard identification card (LincPass) for physical access to federally controlled facilities. ePACS includes the following functions: (a) Issuance based on sound criteria for verifying an individual identity.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: (b) Strong resistance to identity fraud, tampering, counterfeiting, and terrorist exploitation.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: (c) Rapid electronic authentication.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: (d) Issuance only by providers whose reliability has been established by an official accreditation process. ePACS operates under the following SORN: USDA/OCIO-2: System name: eAuthentication Services (March 7, 2017, 82 FR 8503), GSA/GOVT-7: System name: Personal Identity Verification Identity (Oct 23, 2015, 80 FR 64416) And USDA/OSSP-1: System name: enterprise Physical Access Controls System.

sentences.text: The completion of United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) is mandated for any rulemaking, program, system, or practice that collects or uses Personally Identifiable Information (PII) under the authority of the E-government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. § 208(b)) and USDA DR 3515-002, PII.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: The PIA is designed to identify risk associated with the use of PII by a system, program, project or practice, and to ensure that vital data stewardship issues are addressed for all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) of Information Technology (IT) systems.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: It also ensures that security and privacy protections are built into an IT system during its development cycle.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: By regularly assessing privacy concerns during the development process, USDA ensures that proponents of a program or technology have taken its potential privacy impact into account from the beginning.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: The PIA also serves to help identify what level of security risk is associated with a program or technology.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: In turn, this allows the Department to properly manage the security requirements under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA).

sentences.text: The completion of United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) is mandated for any rulemaking, program, system, or practice that collects or uses Personally Identifiable Information (PII) under the authority of the E-government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. § 208(b)) and USDA DR 3515-002, PII.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: The PIA is designed to identify risk associated with the use of PII by a system, program, project or practice, and to ensure that vital data stewardship issues are addressed for all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) of Information Technology (IT) systems.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: It also ensures that security and privacy protections are built into an IT system during its development cycle.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: By regularly assessing privacy concerns during the development process, USDA ensures that proponents of a program or technology have taken its potential privacy impact into account from the beginning.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: The PIA also serves to help identify what level of security risk is associated with a program or technology.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: VERSION 1.4 OFFICE OF THE CHIEF PRIVACY OFFICER The completion of USDA Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) is mandated for any rulemaking, program, system, or practice that collects or uses PII under the authority of the E-government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. § 208(b)) and USDA DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: The PIA is designed to identify risk associated with the use of PII by a system, program, project or practice, and to ensure that vital data stewardship issues are addressed for all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) of IT systems.

sentences.text: It also ensures that security and privacy protections are built into an IT system during its development cycle.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: By regularly assessing privacy concerns during the development process, USDA ensures that proponents of a program or technology have taken its potential privacy impact into account from the beginning.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: The PIA also serves to help identify what level of security risk is associated with a program or technology.

sentences.text: The NAD Tracking System (NADTrack) name is owned by the US Department of Agriculture, Office of Hearings and Appeals (OHA)-National Appeals Division (NAD).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: NADTrack is a Web-based case management, tracking and reporting system used to retain and retrieve case information and report performance statistics based on data entered into the system.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: A typical transaction is OHA-NAD case-related data, audio files and determinations as well as participant and agency contact and/or identifier information is record within the system.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: NADTrack is completely self- contained and does not share data with any other applications except for authentication and access through USDA eAuthentication (eAuth).

sentences.text: To carry out its wide-ranging responsibilities, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and its employees and managers have access to diverse and complex automated information systems, which include system, file servers, local and wide area networks running various platforms, and telecommunications systems to include communication equipment.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The USDA relies on its information technology systems, including the Time and Attendance application (WebTA) to accomplish its mission of providing cost-effective and reliable services to the USDA and other serviced Federal agencies.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The NFC Government Employees Services Division (GESD), which falls under the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), is responsible for development, deployment, maintenance, and testing of the NFC WebTA major application (MA).

sentences.text: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted to fulfill the requirements of Section 208 of Public Law 107-347 (the E-Government Act of 2002).
