sentences.text: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA)Video Surveillance System (VSS) is built on a COTS Application Avigilon Control Center.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The system is designed to capture, view and replay video footage within the National Capitol Region (NCR).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The PIA is being conducted because the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The mission of USDA Office of Safety, Security and Protection (OSSP) Video Surveillance System (VSS) is to keep property safe and secure for federal employees; to provide a costeffective method to monitor a location, provide archived video coverage for investigations; and to deter against future crime or attack.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: OSSP is responsible for the protection of federal facilities, staff, and visitors, which may be the target of acts of terrorism or other crimes such as robbery, burglary or vandalism.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Crimes in progress may be detected and possibly prevented since the video feeds can be monitored in real-time.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Also, a clearly visible camera alerts the public that they are being monitored, which may deter criminal activity.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS supports OSSP's compliance efforts for the video surveillance components of the.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS is owned and operated by USDA Data Administration (DA)/OSSP/Facility Projection Division (FPD).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS provides a secure and cost-effective means for OSSP to deploy video surveillance for the NCR; supports the mitigation of identified threats and vulnerabilities; and assists in assuring unauthorized individuals do not gain access to critical USDA assets.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Additionally, VSS will assist OSSP with its role in securing and protecting the USDA NCR by being a force multiplier for on-site security services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS is built on a Commercial off the Shelf (COTS) product, Avigilon Access Control Center (ACC) and can utilize any analog or IP based camera for collecting video footage.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS allows for the recording, live viewing, archiving and playback of recorded video for electronic surveillance applications.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS performs viewing, playback, and video storage functions simultaneously.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS is an open standard, network-based software platform that is user friendly for both officers and administrators alike.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS is designated an industrial control system, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (ICS/SCADA) system (NIST SP 800-82).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Privacy protections for VSS systems include limiting access to the video feed to only authorized users and establishing clear auditing systems so every use of the VSS system is logged and reviewable and restricting storage.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Also, USDA OSSP VSS users agree to a 'Rules of Behavior' which subjects employees to administrative and potentially criminal penalties if any misuse occurs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS collects and stores streams of video images by location, date, and time.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: VSS captures images on video.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Surveillance cameras are meant to keep people and property secure.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Cameras are there not to invade a person's privacy, but to protect the public by deterring criminal activity and by providing material evidence when a crime has been caught on video.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Office of Customer Experience (OCX) Voice of the Customer (VoC) Medallia tool provides a unified experience management system, through the Medallia Experience Cloud.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This tool will allow Mission Area clients to capture in-the-moment customer feedback via numerous methods, including email surveys, receipt codes, SMS, and QR Code.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The PIA is being conducted as the system may stores PII depending on the Mission Area using the tool and the information collected in the surveys.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The USDA's Office of Customer Experience is working collaboratively with USDA mission areas and offices to continue improving service levels with USDA's customers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: It is being supported through USDA department-wide efforts to understand USDA customer feedback.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Voice of the Customer (VoC) platform by Medallia is a fully-functional enterprise tool designed to assist the USDA to launch a comprehensive customer experience assessment platform, enabling staff to work with large volumes of customer survey and feedback data to analyze results across all USDA mission areas and offices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The VoC tool will enable USDA staff to visualize feedback results in dynamic dashboards and allow actionable feedback for USDA officials.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The VoC tool is designed to collect survey data across all the USDA mission areas.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The data is structured or unstructured, solicited, or unsolicited feedback from customers through multiple channels, including but not limited to surveys, web forms, email, contact centers, in-person visits, and social media.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This feedback will be collected in real-time across a customer's journey and will be placed in the VoC tool.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The tool will support expansion of Voice of the Customer capabilities into other agencies and mission areas.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: In addition to launching the VoC tool, appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: All appropriate security and accessibility measures will be implemented to limit, and control access based on user's roles and permission levels.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is for the USDA, Assistance Chief Financial Officer Financial Management Systems (ACFO-SS-FMS) Workiva system.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The Workiva Wdesk Software as a Service (SaaS) allows customers to collaborate and share documents hosted in the cloud, giving teams the ability to create and edit in real-time from any location.

sentences.text: The PIA was conducted because the Workiva Wdesk system stores usda.gov email address which is considered Personally Identifiable Information (PII) within the cloud provided solution.

sentences.text: This document is a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for the FNS Financial Management General Support System (FNS FM-GSS).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: FNS FM-GSS includes subsystems and applications that the Agency leverages to gather, process, and report on financial data.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The FM-GSS includes the financial applications and supporting platforms, which are hosted within the Microsoft (MS) Azure FedRAMP cloud environment.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The PIA is being completed due to a Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) that indicated a PIA was required for the following subsystems located within the FNS FM-GSS ATO boundary: the Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT) and the Grants Information Management System (GIMS).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The FNS FM-GSS includes the financial applications and supporting platforms, which are hosted within the Microsoft (MS) Azure FedRAMP cloud environment.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: MS Azure FedRAMP is a Government FedRAMP approved cloud environment hosted in geographically-distributed MS Azure datacenters within the U.S. and is built on platforms implementing robust and scalable architectural standards.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Azure provides several security controls, including, but not limited to border protection mechanisms, a redundant DNS architecture, and physical security protections.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The established Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC) Azure tenant and the Cloud Service broker, is a representative for the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) in Azure Active Directory, enables a Departmental managed approach to common controlled services for any agency opting to use Azure Government.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: DISC maintains a security system, and related technical services named the USDA Azure Cloud System, in which the GSS inherits.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The FNS FM-GSS establishes and maintains its Azure subscriptions within this tenant that defines the basic boundary of the FNS FM-GSS.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The FNS FM-GSS ATO boundary includes the following subsystems covered under this PIA.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: FMAT is a Financial Management Support Solution that includes web-based custom-designed applications residing on the FNS intranet.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: It is comprised of the following applications: Automated Entity Resolution and Optimization System (AEROS) is a custom solution providing the repository and mechanism for users to identify and match incoming collections to the appropriate customer and accounts receivable (AR) document.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: It provides a user interface for AR processors to view AR and collection-related data gathered from various systems, confirm data matches made by the system, and track and report on the status of collections throughout their lifecycle.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: Budget User Desktop Solution (BUDS) is an internal FNS web-interface module that provides a process-driven SF-132 budget execution tool for end-users.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: BUDS enables end users to post SF-132 accounting events to the sub-allotment level and presents data in a user-friendly graphical interface.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: Integrated Data Extraction and Analysis (IDEA) is a user-definable data extraction and analysis tool to supplement the existing reporting and analysis capabilities of FMAT.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: The primary objective of this application is to automate the data extraction and validation processes of financial data.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: Grant Award Document and Letter of Credit (GAD/LOC) Amendments Process (GLAP) provides FNS grantees with an Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) version of their GAD/LOC amendments.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: The reports have been electronically signed and dated by an authorized FNS employee in the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI).
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: The FMAT Interface Module supports the exchange of data between BUDS, IDEA, AEROS, GLAP, and the FMMI.
sentences.heading: Financial Management Application Toolset (FMAT)

sentences.text: GIMS is a Document Management product that facilitates the management of all types and formats of content.
sentences.heading: Grants Information Management System (GIMS)

sentences.text: It provides a secure, central repository for organizing and sharing content in an enterprise-wide fashion.
sentences.heading: Grants Information Management System (GIMS)

sentences.text: It includes a flexible and powerful metadata categorization to enrich content by structured data in order to create custom properties, control document status, and support content search and retrieval.
sentences.heading: Grants Information Management System (GIMS)

sentences.text: GIMS also has the capability to check-in/check-out documents; manage version control for simple and compound documents; track audit trails; perform comprehensive searches; and manage user, group, and role-based access controls.
sentences.heading: Grants Information Management System (GIMS)

sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The SNAP Information Database is an initiative of USDA's Office of the Secretary that will leverage datasharing across federal and state systems to identify and rectify any ineligible, duplicate, or fraudulent Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP ) enrollments.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: In addition, this initiative will focus on detecting duplicate enrollments across states, verifying immigration status eligibility, and performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies .
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The SNAP Information Database will collect SNAP participant data (including personal information and transactional data) from all 53 SNAP state agencies via their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) payment processors, through secure channels , to be stored in a database that is then used to perform integrity checks that include, but may not be limited to: Duplicate enrollment (multi -state); Identity and social security number (SSN) validation ; Immigration status check ; Age and household composition validation ; and Inter-Agency data matches I ntegrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database , using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: States will transmit data from 2020 to present, with quarterly updates thereafter.

sentences.heading: External Information Sharing

sentences.text: 6.4. List the privacy risks and mitigations r elated to external information sharing and disclosure.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Follow this format: Privacy Risk : Privacy Act risks associated with sharing information externally include: Unauthorized Access: Sharing PII with third parties increases the risk of unauthorized access, especially if those parties do not have adequate security measures in place.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Data Breaches: External sharing can lead to data breaches, either through hacking or inadvertent exposure, resulting in unauthorized individuals gaining access to sensitive information.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Loss of Control: Once PII is shared externally, the SNAP Information Database and USDA may lose control over how that information is used, which can lead to misuse or unauthorized applications of the data.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Noncompliance with Regulations: Sharing PII without proper consent or outside the parameters set by privacy laws can result in legal penalties and reputational damage.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Inconsistent Data Management Practices: Different third parties may have varying practices for handling PII, leading to inconsistencies in data protection and increased risks.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Insufficient Due Diligence: Failing to conduct proper due diligence on third parties before sharing PII can expose the SNAP Information Database to risks associated with partnering with unreliable or non -compliant entities.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Public Perception and Trust Erosion: External sharing of PII, especially if not communicated transparently, can lead to public distrust and negative perceptions of the SNAP Information Database or agency.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Reputational Damage: I f shared PII is misused or leads to negative outcomes for individuals, it can result in significant reputational harm to the SNAP Information Databas e or agency responsible for the data.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Limited Individual Awareness: Individuals may not be fully aware of how their PII is being shared or the potential risks involved, leading to a lack of informed consent.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Legal Liability: The SNAP Information Database and USDA may face lawsuits or legal actions if individuals believe their PII has been mishandled or improperly disclosed, resulting in financial and operational impacts.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Mitigation : Implementing the following mitigation actions, the SNAP Information Database can manage the risk associated with external sharing and disclosure of personal information while complying with Privacy Act requirements.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Access Controls: Implement strict access controls to ensure that only authorized personnel can share or disclose PII externally.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Security Measures: Employ robust security measures, such as encryption and secure transfer protocols, when sharing personal data to protect it during transmission.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Data Sharing Policy: Develop a clear policy outlining the conditions under which PII can be shared externally, including legal and compliance requirements (ex.: Computer Matching Agreements, SORNs, Business Agreements).
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Due Diligence: Conduct thorough due diligence on third parties before sharing personal data, ensuring their privacy standards and practices are comparable to the PA and USDA requirements.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Written Agreements: Establish written agreements or contracts with third parties that outline their responsibilities for safeguarding shared data and compliance with privacy laws.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Need -toKnow Basis: Limit the sharing of PII to only what is necessary for the intended purpose, adhering to the principle of data minimization.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Individual Consent: Obtain explicit consent from individuals before sharing their personal information with third parties.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Transparency with Individuals: Clearly inform individuals about potential external sharing of their personal data in privacy notices, including the types of entities with whom data may be shared and the purposes for sharing.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Access Controls: Implement strict access controls to ensure that only authorized personnel can share or disclose PII externally.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Individual Consent: Obtain explicit consent from individuals before sharing their personal information with third parties.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Regular Audits: Conduct regular audits of data sharing practices and third -party compliance to ensure adherence to privacy policies and legal requirements.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Incident Response Plan: Develop an incident response plan that outlines procedures for addressing potential data breaches or unauthorized disclosures related to external sharing.
sentences.heading: External Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.heading: Section 7 : Redress

sentences.text: Data being shared is already provided by individuals to SNAP State agencies for the purpose of determining a household's eligibility for SNAP benefits.
sentences.heading: 7.1. What are the procedures that allow individuals to gain access to their information?

sentences.text: Individuals may request data from their State agency who is responsible for collecting and maintaining it.
sentences.heading: 7.1. What are the procedures that allow individuals to gain access to their information?

sentences.text: Any individual that receives a notice of adverse action from a State agency that would impact the household's eligibility or benefit allotment has the right to request a fair hearing per the regulations at 7 CFR 273.15. Existing regulations requires State agencies to present all information used to make a decision and provides procedures for the individual to dispute any inaccurate or erroneous information.
sentences.heading: 7.2. What are the procedures for correcting inaccurate or erroneous information?

sentences.text: State agencies must send a notice of adverse action to any individual based on any action by the State agency to reduce or terminate an individual's SNAP benefit based on a data match or any other source of information, per 7 CFR 273.13 of the regulations.
sentences.heading: 7.3. How are individuals notified of the procedures for correcting their information?

sentences.text: Not applicable.
sentences.heading: 7.4. If no formal redress is provided, what alternatives are available to the individual?

sentences.text: 7.5. List the privacy risks and mitigations r elated to redress.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Follow this format: Privacy Risk : Privacy Act risks associated with redress include: Inadequate Processes: If the processes for individuals to seek redress for privacy violations are unclear or cumbersome, it can deter individuals from exercising their rights and lead to unresolved complaints.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Lack of Transparency: Not providing clear information about how redress mechanisms work can create confusion and mistrust among individuals regarding their rights and the agency's accountability.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Failure to Address Complaints: The SNAP Information Database or agencies may not adequately address or resolve complaints related to privacy violations, leading to dissatisfaction and potential legal repercussions.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Delayed Responses: Slow responses to redress requests can frustrate individuals and exacerbate feelings of mistrust and dissatisfaction, potentially leading to reputational harm.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Inconsistent Application: If redress processes are applied inconsistently across different cases or agencies, it can lead to perceptions of unfairness and bias, undermining trust in the entire department.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Insufficient Recordkeeping: Poor documentation of redress requests and outcomes can hinder an agency's ability to identify patterns of violations, learn from mistakes, and improve practices.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Legal Exposure: Failing to provide adequate redress options may expose the SNAP Information Database or USDA to legal challenges, including lawsuits or regulatory scrutiny, especially if individuals feel their rights have been violated.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Reputation Damage: Public knowledge of inadequate redress mechanisms can damage the department's reputation, leading to loss of customer trust and potential business impacts.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Lack of Accountability: Without effective redress mechanisms, the SNAP Information Database or USDA may not be held accountable for privacy violations, which can perpetuate poor data handling practices.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Discrimination: If redress mechanisms are not accessible to all individuals equally, it may lead to discrimination, where certain groups may find it harder to seek and obtain redress.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Mitigation : To mitigate redress risks, the SNAP Information Database must establish clear, accessible, and effective redress mechanisms, providing transparent information about the process, ensuring timely responses, and maintaining thorough documentation of all complaints and resolutions.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Implementing the following mitigati on actions, the SNAP Information Database can enhance redress mechanisms, ensuring individuals have effective means to address privacy concerns.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Establish Clear Procedures: Develop and communicate clear procedures for individuals to submit complaints or requests for redress related to privacy violations.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: User Awareness Campaigns: Educate users about their rights under the privacy act and the available redress mechanisms through workshops, newsletters, or online resources.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Dedicated Point of Contact: Appoint dedicated personnel who are responsible for handling redress requests and ensuring timely responses to complaints.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Timely Response Protocols: Implement protocols for acknowledging and responding to redress requests promptly, ensuring that individuals feel heard and valued.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Investigation Processes: Create structured process for investigating redress requests, including gathering necessary information and documenting findings.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Remediation Options: Offer various remediation options, such as data correction, deletion, or compensation, depending on the nature of the complaint and the organization's policies.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Feedback Mechanisms: Establish feedback channels for individuals to provide insights on the redress process, helping to improve the system continuously.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Regular Training: Provide ongoing training for employees on handling privacy complaints and the importance of adhering to redress procedures.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Monitoring and Reporting: Regularly monitor redress requests and outcomes to identify trends, potential issues, and areas for improvement in privacy practices.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Analysis

sentences.text: Transparency in Outcomes: Communicate the outcomes of redress requests to the individuals involved, ensuring transparency and fostering trust in the process.

sentences.text: The Affiliates (Affiliates) application is a system of the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The Affiliates application provides a way for authorized NRCS employees to facilitate the process of access control determinations to NRCS systems and applications for select nonNRCS personnel (known as 'affiliates') A Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) was performed, indicating that a PIA must be completed.
sentences.heading: Abstract

Abstract

sentences.text: Affiliates is a system of the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: NRCS provides private landowners with advice, guidance and technical services to carry out conservation practices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The NRCS is an agency within the USDA that has provided over 75 years of leadership in a partnership effort to help America's private land owners and managers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: NRCS works with its partners to conserve their soil, water, and other natural resources by providing financial and technical assistance based on sound science and technology suited to a customer's specific needs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Affiliates is an application that manages access privileges for non-Federal employees or Affiliates of NRCS.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Affiliates are non-employees, typically contractors, who perform services, act on behalf of the government organization, or whose duties on behalf of the government organizations require them to have similar access privileges as government employees.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: When establishing authorization privileges for affiliates to access government information and to use government systems, it is essential that the identity of the person be known to NRCS, as well as information about the organization they represent and the current status of their relationship with USDA.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This information is stored and maintained in the Affiliates Database.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The various county-based agencies have a number of affiliates, including contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Governments, RC&D employees, volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organizations.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: While there are many types of nonemployees, it must be stressed that none of these "affiliates" has any form of access to the Affiliates application itself.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: A typical Affiliates transaction is as follows: An NRCS employee enters the Affiliates information into the Affiliates database.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The zRoles application is then used to assign specific roles to the Level 2 account, which allows the affiliate access to various NRCS applications.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Single Sign-On (SSO) 'eAuth' accounts are used for non-privileged access.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The Affiliates application does not update or modify the eAuth Active Directory in any way.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: While information in the Affiliates application is not transmitted or shared with any other organizations, automated "sharing" does occur between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The zRoles application does not update or modify the Affiliates database in any way.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: NRCS applications or systems contact zRoles to verify the level of authorization granted to affiliates to access their systems.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This PIA addresses the Collaborative Software Development Laboratory (CoLab) application, which is a system of the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS).
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: CoLab manages the changes, revisions, upgrades, and modifications that NRCS-ITC applications undergo throughout the software development life cycle (SDLC), by implementing a formal, documented, systematic process for requesting, evaluating, tracking, and approving changes to these applications.

sentences.text: CoLab is the Internet-based "Collaborative Software Development Laboratory," which is Intland Software's industry standard Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software application based upon the codeBeamer ALM (Application Lifecycle Management) platform.

sentences.text: The NRCS Integrated Data for Enterprise Analysis (IDEA) application provides integrated agency reports and analysis tools for NRCS employees.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The purpose of IDEA is to provide access to comprehensive, integrated business intelligence (BI) to provide for the access, analysis and reporting of NRCS data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: IDEA produces financial reports for the costing and budgeting of conservation practices.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Some of these financial reports contain vendor PH that is obtained from the Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS) system via read-only web service calls.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The PII obtained from SCIMS consists of names and contact information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Some of these IDEA reports rely upon transitory read-only vendor PII that is obtained from SCIMS via web service calls, noting that this transitory PH is not maintained in the application database.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: IDEA does not collect any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from any person.
sentences.heading: Important notes:

sentences.text: While IDEA does not process any transactions, the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
sentences.heading: Important notes:

sentences.text: IDEA does not provide any functionality to retrieve records about individuals by reference to any type of personal identifier.
sentences.heading: Important notes:

sentences.text: NRCS does not, in fact, retrieve records about any individuals from the IDEA database by any reference to any personal identifier.
sentences.heading: Important notes:

sentences.text: IDEA does not process any financial transactions.
sentences.heading: Important notes:

sentences.text: Finally the system provides technical safeguards to prevent misuse of data including; · Confidentiality: Encryption is implemented to secure data at rest and in transit for this application (e.g., by FIPS 140-2 compliant HTTPS and end-user hard disk encryption). o Integrity: Masking of applicable information is performed for this application (e.g., passwords are masked by e-Auth). o Access Control: The systems implements least privileges and need to know to control access to PIT (e.g., by RBAC). o Authentication: Access to the system and session timeout is implemented for this application (e.g. by e-Auth and via multi-factor authentication for remote access). o Audit: Logging is implemented for this application (e.g. by logging infrastructure). o Attack Mitigation: The system implements security mechanisms such as input validation.

sentences.text: The following questions are intended to define the scope of the information requested and/or collected as well as reasons for its collection as part of the program, system, rule, or technology being developed.
sentences.heading: Section 1.0 Characterization of the Information

sentences.text: DamWatch contains Emergency Action Plans (EAPs) that will be activated in the event of an emergency involving an NRCS-managed dam.

sentences.text: The Digital Record Management System (DRMS) is a cloud system that resides on FPAC_AWS_Shared_GSS (FPAC_AWS_GSS).
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: DRMS replaces manual, paper-based document management business processes with a comprehensive digital record management system able to support the end-to-end lifecycle of both permanent and temporary records.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: With NARA-compliance in mind, DRMS acts as the system of record for both electronic records and the metadata necessary to describe those records.

sentences.text: DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.

sentences.text: Name of the component and system: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) Brief description of the system and its function: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) is an Intranet web-based program developed to assist authorized agency officials in determining and evaluating the effects of primary loan servicing in accordance with FSA Handbook 5-FLP. eDALR$ completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: This information is used in attempting to restructure the borrower's debt and maximize their repayment ability, while avoiding or minimizing loss to the Government.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: Why the PIA is being conducted: To support federal law, regulations and policies.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: System Name: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) Agency: FSA System Purpose: a web based application (support tool) to be used by field office employees to assist in computing a debt restructuring plan.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Web enabled version of eDALR$ performs debt and loan restructuring analysis on distressed borrowers or delinquent government loans and went into production in April 2008. Functionality includes: Determining and evaluating the effects of primary loan servicing Completing a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information Restructuring the borrower's debt and maximize their repayment ability Accessing various other web applications for information.

sentences.text: Name of the component and system: Farm Business Plan (FBP) (Web Equity Manager) (FBP) The Farm Business Plan (Web Equity Manager) (FBP) is a web-based application used by USDA Field Service Centers to assist borrowers with obtaining Farm Home Loans and improving their farming business.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The FBP system provides a web-based automated business process from the borrower's initial request for a loan to the county agent's classification of the borrower account and the loan officers' approval of the request.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: A completed FBP provides the business's financial condition, operating plans, and actual summary for a specified time as well as interaction with the Direct Loan Making, Direct Loan Servicing, FLPRA and eDALR$ systems to ensure that loan requests have approved Farm Business Plans and to provide those systems with business data.

sentences.text: System Name: Farm Loan Appraisal System (FLAS) System Description: The Farm Loan Appraisal System (FLAS) provides County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals in support of Direct and Guaranteed loans.
sentences.heading: Overview
Overview

sentences.text: The purpose is to provide County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members with the means to facilitate and track status of appraisals in support of Direct, Guaranteed, and FSFL loans.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Some of the features include capability for preparing and processing customer work orders, ordering in-house or reviewing guaranteed and 3rd party appraisals, forms preparation (Form 2128(PLCE funding), 2165(RE Admin Review), 2167(Chattel Review) and 2234(FSA Review of Lenders Evaluation of Collateral), team member task action reminder notifications, document management (approval tracking, action alerts, case file storage, etc.), and centralizing information allowing for robust analysis and reporting.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The enterprise web application will help to standardize the loan appraisal process and give the FLP community a user-friendly tool to aid in day to day activities. |

sentences.text: System Name: Farm Loan Delivery and Credit Analysis System (FLD CAS) System Description: Farm Loan Delivery and Credit Analysis System (FLD CAS) is comprised of multiple web-based applications that provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications and allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: | Applications | Overview | |------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Direct Loan System (DLS) | DLS resides on Midrange Systems and is a web-based application that provides field offices with the ability to process loan applications using the Loan Making application, service loans using the Loan Servicing application, and allow producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information. | | Electronic Debt & Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) | Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) resides on Midrange Systems and is an intranet web-based program developed to assist authorized agency officials in determining and evaluating the effects of primary loan servicing in accordance with FSA Handbook 5-FLP.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The eDALR$ system completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This information is used in attempting to restructure the borrower's debt and maximize their repayment ability, while avoiding or minimizing loss to the Government.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Web enabled version of eDALR$ performs debt and loan restructuring analysis on distressed borrowers or delinquent government loans and went into production in April 2008. | | Farm Business Plan (Web Equity Manager) (FBP) | Farm Business Plan (FBP) resides on Midrange Systems and is a web-based application used by USDA Field Service Centers to assist borrowers with obtaining Farm Loans and improving their farming business.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The FBP application provides web-based automated business processes that perform farm planning and analysis, loan origination and servicing functions, and manages the FLP loan portfolio.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: A completed FBP provides the business's financial condition, operating plans, and actual summary for a specified time as well as interaction with the Loan Making, Loan Servicing, FLPRA and eDALR$ applications to ensure that loan requests have approved Farm Business Plans and to provide those applications with business data. |

sentences.text: VERSION 1.4 OFFICE OF THE CHIEF PRIVACY OFFICER The completion of USDA Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) is mandated for any rulemaking, program, system, or practice that collects or uses PII under the authority of the E-government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. § 208(b)) and USDA DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: The PIA is designed to identify risk associated with the use of PII by a system, program, project or practice, and to ensure that vital data stewardship issues are addressed for all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) of IT systems.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: It also ensures that security and privacy protections are built into an IT system during its development cycle.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: By regularly assessing privacy concerns during the development process, USDA ensures that proponents of a program or technology have taken its potential privacy impact into account from the beginning.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: The PIA also serves to help identify what level of security risk is associated with a program or technology.
sentences.heading: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE

sentences.text: In turn, this allows the Department to properly manage the security requirements under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA).

sentences.text: The Farm Program Business Partner & Farm Records System (MIDAS) supports various United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Farm Service Agency (FSA) programs.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: These programs provide funds for maintenance and incremental improvements.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The MIDAS Project was established to modernize initiatives to provide a secure, long-term, web-based solution to simplify, integrate, and automate the delivery of Farm Programs across the United States.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The PIA is being conducted because this system contains PII.
sentences.heading: Abstract

sentences.text: The overview is the most important section of the PIA.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: A thorough and clear overview gives the reader the appropriate context to understand the responses in the PIA.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: MIDAS CRM is owned by USDA's FSA Program Delivery Division.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The business purpose of the information technology (IT) system is to capture producer and farm records data for farmers and ranchers in the US who have requested to participate in Farm Service Agency (FSA), National Resource Conservation System (NRCS), and other USDA agencies per program requirements.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This relates to FSA's mission to serve farmers ranchers, and agricultural partners through the delivery of effective, efficient agricultural programs for all Americans.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The system was created to modernize initiatives to provide a secure, long-term, web-based solution to simplify, integrate, and automate the delivery of Farm Programs across the United States to support various USDA programs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities, who voluntarily provided their customer data on an OMB approved form prior to, or during a program application process. .
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: The majority of these individuals and entities have previously participated or are currently participating in USDA programs.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: This system consists of 4 applications which include: Farm Records - this application views, establishes, and maintains farm records data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Business Partner - this application accesses and maintains Business Partner data from a single system of record for all FSA customers.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Product Master - this application captures crop information and provides a full crop catalog.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Organizational Structure this application centralizes CRM employee access and roles to associated counties and positions from source systems.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These applications are accessible via the MIDAS Portal and authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user's create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Together these capabilities form a common system for a significant portion of FSA's core farm and producer data.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These systems integrate with USDA and FSA web-based systems, improve data integrity and security, and ease producer burden by allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data which is shared with other applications and agencies across USDA using shared services.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: These secure and modernized systems support farm program delivery and integrated business processes which are used every day in FSA's 2,124 FSA offices to manage approximately 14 million producers, 5 million farms, 8.1 million tracts, and 38 million fields.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: MIDAS does not operate on more than one site.
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Follow the format below: Privacy Risk : Privacy risks associated with external sharing and disclosure include: Unauthorized Access: Sharing PII with third parties increases the risk of unauthorized access, especially if those parties do not have adequate security measures in place.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Data Breaches: External sharing can lead to data breaches, either through hacking or inadvertent exposure, resulting in unauthorized individuals gaining access to sensitive information.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Loss of Control: Once PII is shared externally, mission areas may lose control over how that information is used, which can lead to misuse or unauthorized applications of the data.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Mitigation : Implementing the following mitigation actions, mission areas can manage the risk associated with external sharing and disclosure of personal information while complying with PA requirements.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Data Sharing Policy: Develop a clear policy outlining the conditions under which PII can be shared externally, including legal and compliance requirements (ex.: Computer Matching Agreements, SORNs, Business Agreements).
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Due Diligence: Conduct thorough due diligence on third parties before sharing personal data, ensuring their privacy standards and practices are comparable to the PA and USDA requirements.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: Written Agreements: Establish written agreements or contracts with third parties that outline their responsibilities for safeguarding shared data and compliance with privacy laws.
sentences.heading: 6.4. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to external sharing and disclosure.

sentences.text: The following questions are directed at an individual's ability to ensure the accuracy of the information collected about him or her.
sentences.heading: Section 7.0 Redress

sentences.text: As published in SORN USDA/FSA-2 and SORN USDA/FSA-14: 'An individual may obtain information about a record in the system which pertains to such individual by submitting a written request to the above listed System Manager.
sentences.heading: 7.1. What are the procedures that allow individuals to gain access to their information?

sentences.text: The envelope and letter should be marked ``Privacy Act Request.'' A request for information should contain: Name, address, ZIP code, name of the system of records, year of records in question, and any other pertinent information to help identify the file.'
sentences.heading: 7.1. What are the procedures that allow individuals to gain access to their information?

sentences.text: As published in SORN USDA/FSA-2 and SORN USDA/FSA-14: 'Individuals desiring to contest or amend information maintained in the system should direct their request to the above listed System Manager and should include the reason for contesting it and the proposed amendment to the information with supporting information to show how the record is inaccurate.
sentences.heading: 7.2. What are the procedures for correcting inaccurate or erroneous information?

sentences.text: A request for contesting records should contain: Name, address, ZIP code, name of the system of records, year of records in question, and any other pertinent information to help identify the file.'
sentences.heading: 7.2. What are the procedures for correcting inaccurate or erroneous information?

sentences.text: Individuals are required to complete a new Customer Data Worksheet AD-2047 to correct their customer information.
sentences.heading: 7.3. How are individuals notified of the procedures for correcting their information?

sentences.text: Individuals can contact any USDA Service Center to request correction to their customer or farm information.
sentences.heading: 7.4. If no formal redress is provided, what alternatives are available to the individual?

sentences.text: Follow the format below: Privacy Risk : Privacy Act risks associated with redress include: Inadequate Processes: If the processes for individuals to seek redress for privacy violations are unclear or cumbersome, it can deter individuals from exercising their rights and lead to unresolved complaints.
sentences.heading: 7.5. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to Redress.

sentences.text: Lack of Transparency: Not providing clear information about how redress mechanisms work can create confusion and mistrust among individuals regarding their rights and the agency's accountability.
sentences.heading: 7.5. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to Redress.

sentences.text: Failure to Address Complaints: Mission areas or agencies may not adequately address or resolve complaints related to privacy violations, leading to dissatisfaction and potential legal repercussions.
sentences.heading: 7.5. PRIVACY IMPACT ANALYSIS: Related to Redress.

sentences.text: Mitigation : Implementing the following mitigation actions, mission areas can enhance redress mechanisms, ensuring individuals have effective means to address privacy concerns.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: Establish Clear Procedures: Develop and communicate clear procedures for individuals to submit complaints or requests for redress related to privacy violations.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: User Awareness Campaigns: Educate users about their rights under the privacy act and the available redress mechanisms through workshops, newsletters, or online resources.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: Dedicated Privacy Officer/Privacy Point of Contact: Appoint a dedicated privacy officer or other personnel responsible for handling redress requests and ensuring timely responses to complaints.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: Timely Response Protocols: Implement protocols for acknowledging and responding to redress requests promptly, ensuring that individuals feel heard and valued.
sentences.heading: Privacy Impact Assessment

sentences.text: System Name: Farm Program Disaster System (FPDS)
sentences.heading: Overview

sentences.text: Farm Program Disaster System (FPDS) provides assistance to eligible farmers and ranchers when a loss occurs as a result of an eligible disaster event, such as flooding, drought, and winter storms.
sentences.heading: System Description:

sentences.text: FPDS contains these applications and components:
sentences.heading: System Description:

sentences.text: The ELAP program will provide emergency relief to producers of livestock, honeybees and farm-raised fish, because of losses from adverse weather or other conditions, such as blizzards and wildfires, as determined by the Secretary.
sentences.heading: 1. Application: Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees, and Farm-Raised Fish Program (ELAP)

sentences.text: This program was authorized by the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008.
sentences.heading: 1. Application: Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees, and Farm-Raised Fish Program (ELAP)

sentences.text: ELAP-Payments provides compensation to eligible producers of livestock, honeybees, and farm-raised fish for losses due to disease, adverse weather, or other loss conditions, including losses due to blizzards and wildfires.
sentences.heading: 1.1 Component of ELAP: Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees, and Farm Raised Fish Program Payments (ELAP-Payments)

sentences.text: LFP was authorized by the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008. The LFP program will be available to eligible livestock producers who suffered grazing losses for eligible livestock, because of drought on land that is either native or improved pastureland with permanent vegetative cover or planted to a crop specifically for providing grazing.
sentences.heading: 2. Application: Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP)

sentences.text: The LFP program will also be available to eligible livestock producers who suffered grazing losses for eligible livestock, because of fire on rangeland managed by a Federal agency, if the eligible livestock producer is prohibited from grazing the normal permitted livestock on the managed rangeland.
sentences.heading: 2. Application: Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP)

sentences.text: With the passage of The Agricultural Act of 2014 (the Act), also known as the 2014 Farm Bill, Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP) has been extended indefinitely (beyond the horizon of the Act).
sentences.heading: 2. Application: Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP)

sentences.text: The program is made retroactive to October 1, 2011. Producers are no longer required to purchase crop insurance or NAP coverage to be eligible for this program.
sentences.heading: 2. Application: Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP)

sentences.text: The LFP-Payments program pays producers authorized for payments through the LFP-Signup software.
sentences.heading: 2.1 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Payments (LFP-Payments)

sentences.text: Processing functions include: Estimated Calculated Report Payment/Overpayment processing Provide for Eligibility, AGI, Direct Attribution, Payment Limitation reductions Process LFP payment and overpayments Interface with NPS Retain producer payment history information Payment History Reporting Support a Non-payment Report Allow for reprocessing of the payment/overpayments
sentences.heading: 2.1 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Payments (LFP-Payments)

sentences.text: The LFP-Signup program, under the 2008 Act, is available to livestock producers who suffered grazing losses for eligible livestock, because of drought on land that is either native or improved pastureland or planted to a crop specifically for grazing.
sentences.heading: 2.2 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Signup (LFP-Signup)

sentences.text: The LFP program will also be available in situations when wildfire prohibits normal grazing on rangeland managed by a Federal agency.
sentences.heading: 2.2 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Signup (LFP-Signup)

sentences.text: To maintain eligibility for LFP, producers must purchase coverage on grazed pasture rather than for all crops in all counties.
sentences.heading: 2.2 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Signup (LFP-Signup)

sentences.text: Processing functions include: Producer signup Producer LFP application form
sentences.heading: 2.2 Component of LFP: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Signup (LFP-Signup)

sentences.text: LIP is an emergency effort administered by the Farm Service Agency (FSA) to help livestock owners who suffered losses from recent natural disasters.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: It provides a partial reimbursement to eligible owners for livestock losses.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: Livestock Indemnity Program assistance is available to eligible owners who suffered livestock losses that were the result of natural disasters or wildfires that received a Presidential Disaster Declaration or Secretarial Disaster Designation.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: Assistance is available only in counties named as primary disaster counties.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: Assistance is not available in contiguous counties under this program.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: Livestock losses due to anthrax are also covered.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: No disaster declaration or designation is required.
sentences.heading: 3. Application: Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP)

sentences.text: The LIP-Payments software pays producers that have signed up for the LIP program.
sentences.heading: 3.1 Component of LIP: Livestock Indemnity Program Payments (LIP-Payments)

sentences.text: Processing functions include: Estimated Calculated Report Payment/Overpayment processing Provide for Eligibility, AGI, Direct Attribution, Payment Limitation reductions Process LIP- payment and overpayments Interface with NPS Retain producer payment history information Payment History Reporting Support a Non-payment Report Allow for reprocessing of the payment/overpayments
sentences.heading: 3.1 Component of LIP: Livestock Indemnity Program Payments (LIP-Payments)

sentences.text: The LIP program, under the 2008 Act compensates producers for livestock death losses in excess of normal mortality due to adverse weather that occurred on or after January 1, 2008. Signup begins when an eligible disaster is apparent.
sentences.heading: 3.2 Component of LIP: Livestock Indemnity Program Signup (LIP-Signup)

sentences.text: Processing functions include: Producer signup Producer LIP application form
sentences.heading: 3.2 Component of LIP: Livestock Indemnity Program Signup (LIP-Signup)

sentences.text: The National crop table is a web-based system that was created to administer and support the 2008-current NAP programs.
sentences.heading: 4. Application: National Crop Table (NCT)

sentences.text: The State Offices enter all pertinent data, including price and yield.
sentences.heading: 4. Application: National Crop Table (NCT)

sentences.text: Crop data records are downloaded daily to the Field Service Centers.
sentences.heading: 4. Application: National Crop Table (NCT)

sentences.text: State Offices can add, update or delete records as needed via the Web.
sentences.heading: 4. Application: National Crop Table (NCT)

sentences.text: This table supports the calculations in the NAP Payment System and other disaster programs as needed.
sentences.heading: 4. Application: National Crop Table (NCT)

sentences.heading: 4.1 Component of NCT: National Crop Table Shared Service (NCTSS)

sentences.text: This allows for reporting of information within the application including the shared data warehouse.
sentences.heading: 4.1 Component of NCT: National Crop Table Shared Service (NCTSS)

sentences.text: Data is retrieved using a SQL process which then provides services for the requesting application.
sentences.heading: 4.1 Component of NCT: National Crop Table Shared Service (NCTSS)

sentences.text: NAP was implemented by the Federal Crop Insurance Reform Act of 1994, as amended by the Agricultural Risk Protection Act of 2000, is a federally funded program that provides financial assistance to producers of non-insurable crops when low yields, loss of inventory, or prevented planting occurs as a result of a natural disaster.
sentences.heading: 5. Application: Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP)

sentences.text: NAP provides coverage for crops for which crop insurance is not available.
sentences.heading: 5. Application: Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP)

sentences.text: AFC enables application coverage to be filed for every producer that wishes to participate in NAP.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: The fees are charged at the pay crop/pay type/planting period level.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: Producers are required to pay the service fee at the time of Application for Coverage.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: The fee data is sent to the accounting system.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: Application for Coverage (AFC) county users enters producer's information.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: If the producer is valid, they select the crop(s) that the producer wants to have covered and collect fee per producer and county pay crop.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: AFC is accessed from FSA Applications and uses eAuthentication to gain access.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: AFC includes NAP Continuous Coverage which is a batch process which generates letters for the KC Print Shop that are physically mailed to NAP producers.
sentences.heading: 5.1 Component of NAP: Application for Coverage (AFC)

sentences.text: A producer must file a NAP application for Payment in order to receive NAP Benefits.
sentences.heading: 5.2 Component of NAP: Application for Payment (AFP)

sentences.text: AFP is used to gather data in order to determine if the producer suffered a loss.
sentences.heading: 5.2 Component of NAP: Application for Payment (AFP)

sentences.text: Calculations and validations of the data are performed, and the approved data is stored to be used by the Payment process.
sentences.heading: 5.2 Component of NAP: Application for Payment (AFP)

sentences.text: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer's Last Name.
sentences.heading: 5.2 Component of NAP: Application for Payment (AFP)

sentences.text: AY was also known as Approved Production History (APH) prior to 2001. A NAP approved yield is established for a producer's unit based on acres and production of a crop/crop type/intended use/planting period/practice.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: In the absence of actual production records, a percentage of the prior year approved yield or percentages of the transitional yield will be used, as applicable.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: The approved yield is used for the application for payment process and other NAP processes as applicable.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: Approved Yields (AY) maintenance can be accessed from the NAP menu.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: 5.4 Component of NAP: Estimated Premium Calculator (EPC) EPC provides the producer with a tool to help calculate the premium cost/acre for NAP buyup.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: This tool is for informational use only and the data is not stored.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: Producers enter data to calculate the premium cost/acre for NAP buy-up.
sentences.heading: 5.3 Component of NAP: Approved Yield (AY)

sentences.text: LAP provides payments for both NAP and TAP Adjuster Vouchers and Travel Fees.
sentences.heading: 5.5 Component of NAP: Loss Adjustor Payments (LAP)

sentences.text: LAV is an automated method for processing, recording, and maintaining Loss Adjuster data, which is the adjustment and inspection services performed for NAP and TAP.
sentences.heading: 5.6 Component of NAP: Loss Adjustor Voucher (LAV)

sentences.text: LAV data is entered through one of two options: Inspection Data or Travel Data.
sentences.heading: 5.6 Component of NAP: Loss Adjustor Voucher (LAV)

sentences.text: This data is used to makes payments through the Voucher Payment Processing for All Programs option.
sentences.heading: 5.6 Component of NAP: Loss Adjustor Voucher (LAV)

sentences.text: A NAP historical marketing percentage (HMP) and/or direct marketing percentage (DMP) is established for a producer electing either of these options along with buy-up coverage on an Application for Coverage.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: Contract marketing data will be collected if applicable and a percentage calculated.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: The CMP, HMP and/or DMP will be used in calculating the loss payment.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: The DMP will be used in calculating the premium.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: Data is collected, and a percentage is calculated for CMP, HMP, and/or DMP.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: CMP and HMP are applicable only if the HMP Option was elected on application for coverage.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: DMP is applicable only if Direct Market Price Option was elected on application for coverage.
sentences.heading: 5.7 Component of NAP: Marketing Percentages (MP)

sentences.text: NAPCC is a batch process within the NAP system which generates letters for the KC Print Shop that are physically mailed to NAP producers.
sentences.heading: 5.8 Component of NAP: NAP Continuous Coverage (NAPCC)

sentences.text: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
sentences.heading: 5.9 Component of NAP: NAP Shared Service (NAP SS)

sentences.text: NAP Shared Service is used to create a new NAP unit as a new acreage report is created in CARS.
sentences.heading: 5.9 Component of NAP: NAP Shared Service (NAP SS)

sentences.text: The NAP SS application is an internal system with no county user interface.
sentences.heading: 5.9 Component of NAP: NAP Shared Service (NAP SS)

sentences.text: Producers who have applied for NAP coverage and satisfied the service fees for the selected crops are eligible for NAP.
sentences.heading: 5.10 Component of NAP: Notice of Loss (NOL)

sentences.text: A timely Notice of Loss must be filed in order for the producer to receive benefits.
sentences.heading: 5.10 Component of NAP: Notice of Loss (NOL)

sentences.text: The notice of loss data is recorded and verified to ensure accuracy.
sentences.heading: 5.10 Component of NAP: Notice of Loss (NOL)

sentences.text: If all the requirements are met for filing the notice of Loss, the Producer must file an Application for Payment in order to receive NAP Benefits.

sentences.text: Notice of Loss (NOL) can be accessed from the NAP menu.
sentences.heading: 5.10 Component of NAP: Notice of Loss (NOL)

sentences.text: This component is documented across multiple NAP Signup systems which need to send notifications (postal letters) to NAP Producers on behalf of FSA county offices.
sentences.heading: 5.11 Component of NAP: Notification Center (NC)

sentences.text: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
sentences.heading: 5.11 Component of NAP: Notification Center (NC)

sentences.text: P/O is a web-based system that interfaces with the National Payment System (NPS) and National Receipts and Receivables System (NRRS).
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: The system utilizes the Common Payment & Reporting Process that was developed for LIP, TAP, and LFP.
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: P/O provides County Office committee approved payments for uninsured crops in the event of an area-wide disaster.
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: Overpayments are calculated similarly.
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: County Offices are required to process overpayments regularly to ensure that all producers are timely notified of outstanding debts.
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: P/O is an automated system that utilizes CPF to perform the following: Payment/Overpayment processing Provide for Eligibility, AGI, Direct Attribution, Payment Limitation reductions Interface with NPS Retain producer payment history information Support a Non-Payment Report Allow for reprocessing of the payment/overpayment
sentences.heading: 5.12 Component of NAP: Payments and Overpayment (P/O)

sentences.text: Premium Management is used to calculate and display producer premium balance due along with previously recorded transactions.
sentences.heading: 5.13 Component of NAP: Premium Management (PM)

sentences.text: The County Office records premium collection data in the System and the system transmits premium collection data to NRRS and stores it.
sentences.heading: 5.13 Component of NAP: Premium Management (PM)

sentences.text: The Supplemental NAP Process is a web-based supplemental application for acreages used for NAP.
sentences.heading: 5.14 Component of NAP: Supplemental NAP Process (SNAPP)

sentences.text: Producers are required to report all acreage of a crop for which they have obtained NAP coverage although some acreage may be considered ineligible for NAP purposes.
sentences.heading: 5.14 Component of NAP: Supplemental NAP Process (SNAPP)

sentences.text: SNAPP will be a means to capture acreage that is ineligible for NAP and maintain the data for multiple NAP processes to use.
sentences.heading: 5.14 Component of NAP: Supplemental NAP Process (SNAPP)

sentences.text: UM is a web-based system used by county offices to create and manage each NAP Unit.
sentences.heading: 5.15 Component of NAP: Unit Maintenance (UM)

sentences.text: UM is required in order to file an application for payment.
sentences.heading: 5.15 Component of NAP: Unit Maintenance (UM)

sentences.text: A NAP unit is based on a unique farming relationship between owners and operators and must be established for every producer that is participating in NAP.
sentences.heading: 5.15 Component of NAP: Unit Maintenance (UM)

sentences.text: The unit structure is used for the approved yield, notice of loss, application for payment processes, and other NAP processes.
sentences.heading: 5.15 Component of NAP: Unit Maintenance (UM)

sentences.text: The Systematic Tracking for Optimal Risk Management (STORM) application is used for logging and tracking information about natural disaster events such as hurricanes, droughts and forest fires that affect agriculture.
sentences.heading: 6 Application: STORM (STORM)

sentences.text: This information is collected by the County Emergency Board (CEB) and submitted in the form of a Loss Assessment Report (LAR) to the State Emergency Board (SEB) for review.
sentences.heading: 6 Application: STORM (STORM)

sentences.text: The SEB has the authority to approve and submit the LAR to the national level where it is used in combination with other LAR information to determine eligibility for disaster relief funds.
sentences.heading: 6 Application: STORM (STORM)

sentences.text: The information collected and submitted in the LAR is the same information being used in the current manual process of drafting Flash Reports and Damage Assessment Reports (DARs) in the county and state offices.
sentences.heading: 6 Application: STORM (STORM)

sentences.text: Processing functions include: Information is collected by the County Emergency Board (CEB) Loss Assessment Report (LAR) submitted to the State Emergency Board (SEB) Approve or Disapproved and submitted to the National level to determine eligibility for disaster relief funds
sentences.heading: 6 Application: STORM (STORM)

sentences.text: The TAP program, authorized by the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008, provides assistance to orchardists and eligible nursery tree growers who produce nursery, ornamental, fruit, nut or Christmas trees for commercial sale that lost trees, bushes, or vines, because of a natural disaster, as determined by the Secretary.
